intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and RAM-model bounds are standard and internally precise, but the record has no inspectable citation. A source with a specific section or page is required.

children.title: Sparse State Maps
children.top_down_role: Keyed storage for state spaces with low reachable-state occupancy.

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse State Maps
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Associative representation storing only reached states and their values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At layer \(t\), let \(R_t\) be the reached states with stored values. A sparse state map contains exactly the key-value pairs \(\{(s,V_t(s)):s\in R_t\}\), inserting a key when first generated and replacing its value when a better transition reaches the same key. A hash-table implementation uses \(\Theta(|R_t|)\) storage and expected \(O(1)\) lookup or update under standard hashing assumptions; an ordered comparison map instead gives \(O(\log |R_t|)\) worst-case lookup and update.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sparse map stores only reached states, using space proportional to occupancy and associative lookup to combine duplicate states.
assumptions_latex: State keys have exact equality and stable hash or comparison operations.
Hash-table expectations assume controlled load and a suitable hashing scheme.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Sparse storage is \(\Theta(|R_t|)\), with expected constant-time hashing or logarithmic comparison-map operations.

notation.meaning: Set of reached states at layer t.
Stored dynamic-programming value for state s.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: standard associative-map storage and operation bounds
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The associative-map representation and conditional operation bounds are mathematically standard, but no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: Density-Adaptive Storage
children.top_down_role: Storage organization responsive to occupancy changes across stages.

knowledge_statements.title: Density-Adaptive Storage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Switches exactly between sparse and dense layer representations using observed occupancy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For layer universe size \(M_t\) and reached-state count \(N_t\), compute density \(\rho_t=N_t/M_t\). Given estimated layer costs \(C_D(M_t)\) for dense storage and \(C_S(N_t)\) for sparse storage, use the representation with smaller estimated cost. When switching, copy every reached pair \((s,V_t(s))\) into the new representation and initialize all other dense entries to the unreachable sentinel. Optionally use two thresholds \(0\le\tau_{SD}<\tau_{DS}\le1\) to prevent repeated switching. Because conversion preserves every reached key and value, representation changes do not alter the recurrence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose sparse or dense storage from observed occupancy and cost, copying all reached values exactly when switching representations.
assumptions_latex: The finite state universe has size \(M_t>0\).
Both representations implement identical lookup and value-combination semantics.
Conversion copies every reached state-value pair exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Cost-based switching preserves all dynamic-programming values; hysteresis thresholds prevent oscillatory conversions.

notation.meaning: Estimated dense and sparse layer costs.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: semantics-preserving conversion between standard state-table representations
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The semantics-preserving conversion algorithm is coherent and correctly placed, but its cost-based switching and hysteresis claims lack an inspectable citation.

children.title: Layered Storage-Reconstruction Tradeoff
children.top_down_role: Stage-layer retention and reconstruction tradeoffs.

children.title: Rolling-Layer Storage
children.top_down_role: Retention limited to stage layers needed for current evaluation.

knowledge_statements.title: Rolling-Layer Storage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Two-layer execution for a finite layered dynamic program whose recurrence uses only the preceding layer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S_0,\ldots,S_T\) be finite state layers, let \(E_t\subseteq S_{t-1}\times S_t\), let \(c_t:E_t\to\mathcal A\), and let \(\oplus\) be an associative operation on \(\mathcal A\) with identity \(0_{\oplus}\). Suppose \(V_0:S_0\to\mathcal A\) is given and, for \(t\ge 1\), the recurrence is \[V_t(s)=\bigoplus_{(u,s)\in E_t}\bigl(V_{t-1}(u)\otimes c_t(u,s)\bigr),\qquad s\in S_t,\] with an empty reduction equal to \(0_{\oplus}\). Store \(V_{t-1}\) in one array, compute \(V_t\) in a second array, and then discard the first array. If one value occupies one word and \(M=\max_{0\le t\le T}|S_t|\), at most \(2M+O(1)\) words are used for values. Discarded predecessor choices are unavailable for direct path reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: When each layer depends only on the preceding layer, keep the preceding and current value arrays and discard older arrays. This uses linear memory in the largest layer but does not retain a complete predecessor trace.
assumptions_latex: \(T<\infty\) and every \(S_t\) is finite.
\(E_t\subseteq S_{t-1}\times S_t\), and each recurrence reads only \(V_{t-1}\).
\(\oplus\) is associative and has an identity for empty reductions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(V_T\) is computed exactly using \(O(M)\) value-storage words.

notation.meaning: transitions from layer t-1 to layer t
transition-data map used by the recurrence
maximum number of states in any layer

children.title: Checkpointed Storage
children.top_down_role: Periodic retention of selected stage layers for later recovery.

knowledge_statements.title: Checkpointed Storage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Periodic checkpointing with blockwise recomputation for reconstructing an optimal path in a layered dynamic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an interval \(k\in\{1,\ldots,T\}\). During the forward dynamic-programming pass, retain complete value layers at indices \(0,k,2k,\ldots,T\), including the final layer. To reconstruct a selected terminal optimum, process checkpoint blocks backward. Starting from the saved value array at a block's left endpoint, recompute that block while retaining its local predecessor choices, trace the selected state to the preceding checkpoint, and then discard the block-local data. With \(M=\max_t|S_t|\), stored checkpoints and one reconstructed block require \(O((\lceil T/k\rceil+k)M)\) words. Each layer is recomputed at most once, so reconstruction adds at most one forward pass of layer evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Store every kth value layer, then recompute one block at a time backward. This reconstructs an optimum with controlled checkpoint memory and at most one extra forward pass.
assumptions_latex: \(T<\infty\), \(1\le k\le T\), and \(|S_t|\le M\).
Each layer is reproducibly computable from its immediate predecessor.
A minimizing predecessor can be stored whenever a block is recomputed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal state path is reconstructed using \(O((\lceil T/k\rceil+k)M)\) words and at most \(T\) additional layer evaluations.

notation.meaning: number of layers per checkpoint block

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: periodic DP checkpoints permit deterministic blockwise recomputation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm, reconstruction assumptions, and asymptotic counts are coherent and fit the checkpointed-storage leaf. The cited locator identifies only a general dynamic-programming chapter and does not specifically support periodic checkpointing, blockwise reconstruction, or the claimed one-pass recomputation bound.

children.title: Reconstruction Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Memory, recovery effort, and solution-trace implications of partial layer retention.

knowledge_statements.title: Reconstruction Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Memory–recomputation bounds for uniform checkpoint intervals in immediate-predecessor layered dynamic programs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose every layer contains at most \(M\) stored values and a solution path must be reconstructed after computing \(T\) layers. Full predecessor storage uses \(O(TM)\) words and requires no layer recomputation. Uniform checkpointing with block length \(k\) stores \(O(\lceil T/k\rceil M)\) checkpoint words and needs \(O(kM)\) temporary words during block reconstruction; its extra work is at most \(T\) layer evaluations. Consequently, choosing \(k=\lceil\sqrt{T}\rceil\) gives \(O(M\sqrt{T})\) storage and \(O(T)\) additional layer work. These bounds count value or predecessor entries as constant-size words.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Full traces use linear-in-horizon layers of memory; square-root checkpoint spacing reduces storage to square-root scale while adding at most one recomputation pass.
assumptions_latex: \(T\ge1\) and \(|S_t|\le M\) for every layer.
The recurrence depends only on the immediately preceding layer.
A layer evaluation has the same asymptotic cost during initial computation and recomputation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Uniform checkpointing realizes storage \(O((T/k+k)M)\), minimized asymptotically at \(k=\Theta(\sqrt{T})\).

notation.meaning: maximum number of stored entries per layer

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the bound follows from counting stored checkpoints and one block of temporary predecessor data
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The complexity-bound role fits the leaf, and the stated checkpoint-memory optimization is mathematically coherent under the listed model. No inspectable source is supplied for the tradeoff or recomputation bound.

children.title: Bit-Parallel State Sets
children.top_down_role: Packed representations for reachability and subset-state propagation.

knowledge_statements.title: Bit-Parallel State Sets
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Word-packed reachability update for nonnegative integer subset-sum states bounded by a capacity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For item weights \(a_1,\ldots,a_n\in\{0,\ldots,B\}\), represent the reachable sums after item \(i\) by a bit vector \(R_i\) of length \(B+1\), where bit \(s\) equals one exactly when sum \(s\) is reachable. Initialize \(R_0=1\), with only bit zero set, and update \[R_i=R_{i-1}\mathbin{\mathrm{OR}}\bigl((R_{i-1}\ll a_i)\mathbin{\mathrm{AND}}(2^{B+1}-1)\bigr).\] On a word-RAM with word length \(w\), each update takes \(O(\lceil(B+1)/w\rceil)\) word operations. Rolling the vectors gives total time \(O(n\lceil(B+1)/w\rceil)\) and memory \(O(\lceil(B+1)/w\rceil)\) words.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pack reachable sums into bits; shifting by an item weight and taking bitwise OR performs many subset-sum transitions per machine operation.
assumptions_latex: \(a_i\) and \(B\) are nonnegative integers.
Bits above index \(B\) are discarded.
The word-RAM supports constant-time shifts, Boolean operations, and adjacent-word carry handling.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The packed recurrence computes all subset-sum reachability states through capacity \(B\) with a factor-\(w\) word-parallel speedup.

notation.meaning: packed reachable-sum set after processing i items

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: this is the standard packed-bit subset-sum recurrence
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The packed subset-sum update is appropriate for the bit-parallel-state-set container and is internally consistent under the word-RAM assumptions. No citation with a specific locator supports the recurrence or complexity bounds.

children.title: Parallel Frontier Processing
children.top_down_role: Concurrent evaluation of independent states, transitions, or label buckets.

knowledge_statements.title: Parallel Frontier Processing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous parallel evaluation of transitions entering one layer of an acyclic dynamic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For layer \(t\), assign transitions \((u,v)\in E_t\) among processors. Each processor computes the candidate \(x_{uv}=V_{t-1}(u)\otimes c_t(u,v)\). Candidates with the same destination are combined by a deterministic reduction \[V_t(v)=\bigoplus_{(u,v)\in E_t}x_{uv}.\] A barrier separates consecutive layers. If \(\oplus\) is associative and commutative, any reduction tree yields the same value as sequential processing. With \(P\) processors and unit-cost candidates, one layer has work \(O(|E_t|)\) and span \(O(\lceil|E_t|/P\rceil+\log d_t)\), where \(d_t\) is the maximum number of transitions entering one state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Evaluate transitions of one frontier concurrently, reduce candidates by destination, and synchronize before advancing. Associative, commutative reduction preserves the sequential dynamic-programming values.
assumptions_latex: \(E_t\subseteq S_{t-1}\times S_t\) is finite.
\(\oplus\) is associative and commutative with an identity.
Layer \(t\) reads only immutable values from layer \(t-1\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The parallel frontier update returns exactly the sequential layer values with \(O(|E_t|)\) work.

notation.meaning: maximum destination indegree in the layer

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: independent transition evaluation followed by associative destination reduction is a standard parallelization of layered DP

children.title: State Relaxation-Refinement Calculus

children.title: Resource-Aggregation Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Coarsening or aggregation of resource coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Aggregation Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Capacity relaxation obtained by rounding nonnegative integer resource consumreitons down to coarser units.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a minimization dynamic program whose paths select transitions \(e\) with nonnegative integer consumptions \(a_e\) and must satisfy \(\sum_e a_e\le B\). For an aggregation unit \(\Delta\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\), replace each consumption by \(\bar a_e=\lfloor a_e/\Delta\rfloor\) and the capacity by \(\bar B=\lfloor B/\Delta\rfloor\). Every exactly feasible path is aggregation-feasible because \[\sum_e\bar a_e\le\left\lfloor\frac{\sum_e a_e}{\Delta}\right\rfloor\le\bar B.\] The converse can fail, so the aggregated state model is a relaxation. If transition costs are unchanged, its optimum is a lower bound on the exact minimization optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round resource consumption down to coarse units. Exact feasible paths remain feasible, additional paths may appear, and the coarsened minimization value is a valid lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(a_e\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\), \(B\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge0}\), and \(\Delta\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\).
The objective is minimized over feasible paths.
Aggregation changes only the resource feasibility test.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{agg}}\le z_{\mathrm{exact}}\).

notation.meaning: exact resource consumption of transition e

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: downward rounding gives a direct feasible-set inclusion and minimization lower bound
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly describes a resource-coordinate relaxation: downward rounding preserves exact feasible paths and gives a minimization lower bound. The scope note contains a typographical error, and no inspectable source is supplied.

children.title: History-Memory Relaxation Family
children.top_down_role: Omission of selected logical, sequencing, or visitation information.

children.title: Logical-Memory Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Relaxations omitting selected logical-state information.

knowledge_statements.title: Logical-Memory Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existential abstraction of finite reachable history states that forgets selected logical distinctions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H_t\) be the finite set of reachable exact history states at layer \(t\), and let \(\alpha_t:H_t\to\bar H_t\) be a surjective abstraction. A relaxed arc \((\bar h,\bar h')\) exists when an exact arc \((h,h')\) satisfies \(\alpha_{t-1}(h)=\bar h\) and \(\alpha_t(h')=\bar h'\). Assign it cost \[\bar c_t(\bar h,\bar h')=\min\{c_t(h,h'):(h,h')\text{ induces }(\bar h,\bar h')\}.\] Every exact path therefore projects to a relaxed path of no greater cost. For additive-cost minimization, \(z_{\mathrm{rel}}\le z_{\mathrm{exact}}\). If every \(\alpha_t\) is injective on \(H_t\), the quotient reproduces the exact reachable-state model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merge reachable histories that agree on retained logical memory, admit every transition induced by a representative, and use the least induced cost. This gives a minimization lower bound and becomes exact when no reachable histories are merged.
assumptions_latex: Each \(H_t\) is finite and consists of reachable exact histories.
Each \(\alpha_t\) is surjective.
The exact problem minimizes additive transition costs, and relaxed arcs use all exact representatives.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_{\mathrm{rel}}\le z_{\mathrm{exact}}\), with exact recovery when every reachable-history abstraction is injective.

notation.meaning: reachable exact history-state set at layer t
minimum induced cost of a relaxed arc

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: existential quotient transitions and minimum representative costs define a minimization relaxation

children.title: Sequencing-History Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Relaxations omitting selected ordering or predecessor information.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequencing-History Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-order suffix abstraction for sequence-dependent dynamic-programming histories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an exact state contain a finite sequence history \(h=(x_1,\ldots,x_t)\) over an alphabet \(X\). For a memory order \(k\ge0\), define \(\alpha_k(h)\) as the suffix of \(h\) having length \(\min\{k,t\}\), and merge histories with the same suffix. Between suffix states, admit every transition induced by at least one pair of representative exact histories and assign the minimum induced transition cost. The model may concatenate transitions whose representatives have incompatible forgotten prefixes, but every exact sequence projects to a relaxed sequence. Thus its additive-cost minimization optimum satisfies \(z_k\le z_{\mathrm{exact}}\). If the horizon is \(T\) and \(k\ge T\), no sequence history is forgotten.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Retain only the last k sequence symbols, admit transitions induced by representatives, and use their minimum induced costs. This gives a minimization lower bound and is exact when k covers the finite horizon.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) and the horizon \(T\) are finite.
The exact objective minimizes additive transition costs.
Relaxed transitions use existential representatives and minimum induced costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_k\le z_{\mathrm{exact}}\), and \(z_k=z_{\mathrm{exact}}\) whenever \(k\ge T\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: suffix-state quotienting specializes logical-memory relaxation

children.title: Visitation-History Relaxations
children.top_down_role: Relaxations omitting selected visitation records.

knowledge_statements.title: Visitation-History Relaxations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Visited-set abstraction that tracks exact membership only for a selected subset of objects.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an exact state contain a visited set \(U\subseteq V\). Choose a tracked subset \(K\subseteq V\) and replace \(U\) by \(\alpha_K(U)=U\cap K\). Merge states when their nonhistory coordinates agree and their intersections with \(K\) coincide. Define relaxed transitions as the union of transitions induced by representatives, assigning each relaxed arc the minimum induced cost. Visitation status for objects in \(V\setminus K\) is forgotten, so the quotient may admit inconsistent revisits. Every exact path projects to a relaxed path, and hence \(z_K\le z_{\mathrm{exact}}\) for additive-cost minimization. Taking \(K=V\) restores the exact visited-set state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Track visitation only for selected objects. Forgetting the other visitation coordinates may admit extra paths, giving a minimization lower bound; tracking every object restores the exact state model.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite and exact states include \(U\subseteq V\).
The exact objective minimizes additive transition costs.
Relaxed arcs use existential representatives and minimum induced costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z_K\le z_{\mathrm{exact}}\), with \(z_V=z_{\mathrm{exact}}\).

notation.meaning: objects whose visitation status is retained

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: projection onto tracked visitation coordinates yields an existential state relaxation

children.title: History-Restoration Regimes
children.top_down_role: Regimes for restoring selected historical distinctions.

knowledge_statements.title: History-Restoration Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone bound recovery under nested refinements of finite history-state partitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each layer \(t\), let \(\Pi_t^0,\ldots,\Pi_t^m\) be partitions of a finite reachable exact-history set \(H_t\), with \(\Pi_t^{j+1}\) refining \(\Pi_t^j\). Construct each quotient using existential representative arcs and minimum representative costs. Every path admitted at level \(j+1\) maps to a path admitted at level \(j\), with no smaller cost at the finer level. Therefore, for additive-cost minimization, \[z^0\le z^1\le\cdots\le z^m\le z_{\mathrm{exact}}.\] If every \(\Pi_t^m\) is the singleton partition of \(H_t\), then \(z^m=z_{\mathrm{exact}}\), and exact feasible histories can be reconstructed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Restoring forgotten history distinctions through nested partition refinements monotonically strengthens minimization bounds and recovers the exact model when every reachable history is separated.
assumptions_latex: Every reachable \(H_t\) is finite.
\(\Pi_t^{j+1}\) refines \(\Pi_t^j\) for every \(t\) and \(j\).
All quotient models minimize additive costs using existential arcs and minimum representative costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(z^0\le z^1\le\cdots\le z^m\le z_{\mathrm{exact}}\), with equality at singleton reachable-history partitions.

notation.meaning: history-state partition at layer t and refinement level j
optimal value at refinement level j

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: refinement of quotient partitions shrinks the relaxed path set and restores exactness at singleton classes

children.title: Width-Limited State Merging
children.top_down_role: State aggregation driven by a prescribed frontier-width limit.

knowledge_statements.title: Width-Limited State Merging
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Existential state aggregation enforcing a prescribed maximum number of frontier states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a width limit \(W\ge1\). At each layer \(t\), if the exact or generated frontier \(S_t\) has more than \(W\) states, choose a partition \(\Pi_t\) of \(S_t\) with at most \(W\) blocks and replace every state by its block. Add an aggregate transition \((B,C)\) whenever some exact transition joins a representative of \(B\) to a representative of \(C\), and assign it cost \[\bar c_t(B,C)=\min\{c_t(u,v):u\in B, v\in C, (u,v)\in E_t\}.\] Run the dynamic program on these aggregate frontiers. Every exact path projects to an aggregate path, so the output lower-bounds the exact minimization optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partition each frontier into at most W aggregate states, retain every representative-induced transition, and use minimum induced costs. The bounded-width model yields a minimization lower bound.
assumptions_latex: \(W\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}\) and every \(S_t\) is finite.
The objective minimizes additive transition costs.
Each aggregate arc uses all exact representative arcs between its endpoint blocks.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every aggregate frontier has width at most \(W\), and \(z_W\le z_{\mathrm{exact}}\).

notation.meaning: partition of states at layer t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: existential partition quotients preserve every exact path while bounding the number of aggregate states
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm matches width-limited state merging, explicitly enforces the width limit, and gives the correct minimization lower-bound direction under existential arcs and minimum representative costs. No source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Iterative State Refinement
children.top_down_role: Progressive restoration of distinctions needed to strengthen a relaxed state model.

knowledge_statements.title: Iterative State Refinement
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample-guided partition refinement of a finite relaxed dynamic-programming state model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize each finite exact layer \(S_t\) with a partition \(\Pi_t^0\) and solve the induced existential quotient relaxation. At iteration \(j\), inspect an optimal relaxed path. If there is a sequence of exact representatives that realizes every selected relaxed transition and its selected cost consistently, return the corresponding exact path. Otherwise identify an aggregate block \(B\in\Pi_t^j\) involved in the incompatibility and choose a predicate whose two nonempty classes separate the responsible incompatible representatives. Replace \(B\) by those classes and resolve. Each proper split refines the quotient without removing exact paths, so for minimization \(z^{j+1}\ge z^j\). If every unsuccessful iteration performs one proper split, at most \[\sum_t\bigl(|S_t|-|\Pi_t^0|\bigr)\] splits occur before all partitions are singletons, at which point the quotient is exact.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Solve a quotient relaxation, test whether its optimum has a consistent exact realization, and split a state class responsible for any incompatibility. Bounds strengthen monotonically, and finite state sets guarantee exactness after finitely many proper splits.
assumptions_latex: Every exact layer \(S_t\) is finite.
Quotient arcs are existential and use minimum representative costs.
Each unsuccessful iteration performs a proper split separating representatives responsible for the diagnosed incompatibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The lower bounds are nondecreasing, and exactness is reached after at most \(\sum_t(|S_t|-|\Pi_t^0|)\) proper splits.

notation.meaning: state partition at layer t in iteration j
relaxed minimization value in iteration j
finite exact state set at layer t

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: proper refinement of finite partitions monotonically removes quotient behaviors and terminates at singleton partitions

children.title: Label-Resource Representation System
children.top_down_role: Information carried by labels and the mechanisms governing resource extension.

children.title: Additive Resource Labels
children.top_down_role: Labels whose numerical resources accumulate additively.

knowledge_statements.title: Additive Resource Labels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines path labels whose resource coordinates are sums of arc consumptions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a directed graph, let \(s\in V\), and assign each arc \(a\in A\) a cost \(c_a\in\mathbb R\) and resource vector \(r_a\in\mathbb R^m\). The additive label of an \(s\)-to-\(v\) walk \(P=(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\) is \(L(P)=(v,C(P),R(P))\), where \[C(P)=\sum_{i=1}^k c_{a_i},\qquad R(P)=\sum_{i=1}^k r_{a_i}.\] Extending \(P\) by an arc \(a=(v,w)\) produces \(L(Pa)=(w,C(P)+c_a,R(P)+r_a)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An additive label records a walk endpoint and the componentwise sums of its arc costs and resource consumptions.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,A)\) is a directed graph with distinguished source \(s\).
Each arc has a real cost and an \(m\)-dimensional real resource vector.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(L(Pa)=(w,C(P)+c_a,R(P)+r_a)\) for every admissible extension \(a=(v,w)\).

notation.meaning: Total cost accumulated along walk P.

children.title: Temporal Feasibility Label Family
children.top_down_role: Labels carrying temporal feasibility and waiting information.

children.title: Time-Window Labels
children.top_down_role: Labels carrying temporal-window feasibility information.

knowledge_statements.title: Time-Window Labels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Earliest-arrival labels for paths subject to vertex time windows.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each vertex \(i\in V\) have a time window \([e_i,\ell_i]\), service duration \(p_i\ge 0\), and let each arc \((i,j)\in A\) have travel time \(t_{ij}\ge 0\). A time-window label for a partial path ending at \(i\) contains a feasible service-start time \(T_i\in[e_i,\ell_i]\). Its extension to \(j\) is \[T_j=\max\{e_j,T_i+p_i+t_{ij}\}.\] The extension is feasible exactly when \(T_j\le \ell_j\); otherwise it is discarded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A time-window label stores service-start time, advances it by service and travel, permits waiting, and rejects arrivals after the latest time.
assumptions_latex: \(t_{ij}\ge 0\) and \(p_i\ge 0\).
Service at every visited vertex must start within its closed time window.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An extension \((i,j)\) is feasible if and only if \(\max\{e_j,T_i+p_i+t_{ij}\}\le\ell_j\).

notation.meaning: Permitted service-start interval at vertex i.
Service-start time represented by the label.
Service duration and arc travel time.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The standard time-window update is plausible and fits the leaf, but no source is cited. A source should also establish the graph context and the intended service-start convention.

children.title: Scheduling Labels
children.top_down_role: Labels carrying schedule-position or temporal-assignment information.

knowledge_statements.title: Scheduling Labels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State representation for dynamic programs that construct schedules incrementally.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For jobs \(J=\{1,\ldots,n\}\), a scheduling label is \(L=(S,\tau,z)\), where \(S\subseteq J\) is the set of completed jobs, \(\tau\) is the current resource-availability state, and \(z\in\mathbb R\) is accumulated objective value. If job \(j\in J\setminus S\) is eligible under the scheduling constraints, an extension map produces \[L'=(S\cup\{j\},F_j(\tau),z+g_j(\tau)).\] A complete schedule is represented by a reachable label with \(S=J\); infeasible extensions are omitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A scheduling label records completed jobs, current availability, and accumulated objective value; eligible job insertions generate successor labels.
assumptions_latex: The job set \(J\) is finite.
The state \(\tau\) contains all information needed to test and update feasibility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reachable terminal labels satisfying \(S=J\) represent complete feasible schedules.

notation.meaning: State update and incremental objective for scheduling job j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Representation is the appropriate content kind, but the generic state and update maps depend materially on the machine environment, eligibility rules, and objective convention. A model-specific source is required.

children.title: Waiting-Time States
children.top_down_role: Label states representing permissible waiting within temporal constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Waiting-Time States
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines the temporal state induced by early arrival and mandatory waiting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a partial path reaches vertex \(j\) at time \(A_j\), and service at \(j\) may not begin before \(e_j\). The waiting-time state is \[W_j=(e_j-A_j)_+=\max\{0,e_j-A_j\},\] and the corresponding service-start time is \(T_j=A_j+W_j=\max\{A_j,e_j\}\). If \(j\) also has latest service-start time \(\ell_j\), the state is feasible exactly when \(T_j\le\ell_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Waiting is the positive difference between earliest permitted service and arrival; adding it yields the earliest feasible service-start time.
assumptions_latex: Arrival time \(A_j\) and earliest service time \(e_j\) are finite.
Waiting at vertex \(j\) is permitted.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(W_j=(e_j-A_j)_+\) and feasibility with window \([e_j,\ell_j]\) is equivalent to \(A_j+W_j\le\ell_j\).

notation.meaning: Waiting time before service at vertex j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The waiting-time identity is mathematically precise and appropriate for the leaf, but the record has no authoritative source for the time-window convention.

children.title: Resource-Extension Function Systems
children.top_down_role: Transition-dependent resource systems beyond purely additive accumulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Extension Function Systems
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generalizes additive resource accumulation through arc-dependent state maps.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \((\mathcal R,\preceq)\) be a partially ordered resource space. A resource-extension function system on \(G=(V,A)\) assigns each arc \(a=(i,j)\) a map \(f_a:D_a\to\mathcal R\), with \(D_a\subseteq\mathcal R\). A partial walk with resource state \(R\in\mathcal R\) can traverse \(a\) exactly when \(R\in D_a\), after which its state becomes \(f_a(R)\). For \(P=(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\), the terminal resource is the composition \(f_{a_k}\circ\cdots\circ f_{a_1}(R_0)\), provided every intermediate state lies in the next map's domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each arc carries a possibly nonlinear partial state-update map; a walk is feasible when every successive map is defined.
assumptions_latex: \((\mathcal R,\preceq)\) is a partially ordered set.
Every arc \(a\) has a specified partial map \(f_a:D_a\to\mathcal R\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The resource of \(P=(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\) is \((f_{a_k}\circ\cdots\circ f_{a_1})(R_0)\) whenever all intermediate extensions are defined.

notation.meaning: Resource-extension map associated with arc a.
Domain of states from which arc a is feasible.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The partial-map formulation fits resource-extension systems, but no source confirms that this is the intended formalism or whether further order-compatibility axioms belong to the definition.

children.title: Logic-Automaton Label Interface
children.top_down_role: Labels carrying admissible-sequence or logical-state information.

children.title: Logical-State Labels
children.top_down_role: Labels carrying Boolean, categorical, or rule-status information.

knowledge_statements.title: Logical-State Labels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boolean-state labels for incrementally enforced logical requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B=\{b_1,\ldots,b_q\}\) be Boolean state variables and \(X=\{0,1\}^q\). A logical-state label for a partial decision sequence \(P\) is \(L(P)=(v,x)\), where \(v\) is its endpoint and \(x\in X\) records the truth valuation relevant to future feasibility. Each admissible action \(a\) has a partial update \(U_a:D_a\to X\). The extension \(Pa\) is logically feasible exactly when \(x\in D_a\), and then \(L(Pa)=(w,U_a(x))\), where \(w\) is the new endpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A logical-state label stores a Boolean valuation sufficient to test and update logical feasibility after each action.
assumptions_latex: The Boolean variable set \(B\) is finite.
The stored valuation is sufficient for future logical-feasibility decisions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Action \(a\) is extendable from state \(x\) if and only if \(x\in D_a\), with successor state \(U_a(x)\).

notation.meaning: Valuations from which action a is logically admissible.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Boolean-state definition fits the leaf, but its key sufficiency requirement and partial-update semantics lack supporting evidence.

children.title: Automaton-State Labels
children.top_down_role: Labels carrying states of a sequence-recognition automaton.

knowledge_statements.title: Automaton-State Labels
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-automaton representation of sequence-dependent label feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal A=(Q,\Sigma,\delta,q_0,F)\) be a deterministic finite automaton, allowing a partial transition function \(\delta:Q\times\Sigma\rightharpoonup Q\). For a partial sequence \(w=\sigma_1\cdots\sigma_k\), its automaton-state label is \(q(w)=\delta^*(q_0,w)\) when the extended transition is defined. Appending \(\sigma\in\Sigma\) is feasible exactly when \(\delta(q(w),\sigma)\) is defined, and the successor label is that state. A complete sequence is accepted exactly when its final label belongs to \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A label stores the finite-automaton state reached by the partial sequence; defined transitions permit extensions, and accepting states certify completion.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal A\) is a deterministic finite automaton with possibly partial transitions.
Sequence symbols belong to the alphabet \(\Sigma\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every sequence \(w\), acceptance is equivalent to \(\delta^*(q_0,w)\in F\), provided the extended transition is defined.

notation.meaning: Transition function extended from symbols to sequences.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation accurately describes labels induced by a deterministic partial automaton, but no source supports its use as the intended dynamic-programming label interface.

children.title: Sequence-Admissibility Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces connecting label states to admissible-sequence restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Sequence-Admissibility Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface condition connecting dynamic-programming extensions to a language recognizer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let feasible complete action sequences be specified by a language \(\mathcal L\subseteq\Sigma^*\), and let \(S\) be a state set with initial state \(s_0\), partial update \(U:S\times\Sigma\rightharpoonup S\), and accepting set \(S_F\subseteq S\). The interface is sequence-admissibility exact when, for every \(w=\sigma_1\cdots\sigma_k\in\Sigma^*\), \[w\in\mathcal L\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad U^*(s_0,w)\text{ is defined and }U^*(s_0,w)\in S_F.\] Thus label extension exposes precisely the state information required to recognize admissible completed sequences.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An interface is exact when iterated label updates end in an accepting state exactly for the admissible sequences.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal L\subseteq\Sigma^*\) is the intended set of admissible complete sequences.
\(U\) is a deterministic partial state update.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(w\in\mathcal L\) if and only if \(U^*(s_0,w)\) is defined and lies in \(S_F\).

notation.meaning: State update extended to finite sequences.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Condition is the correct content kind and the recognition equivalence is precise, but the proposed interface definition has no cited source.

children.title: Single-Resource Constrained Paths
children.top_down_role: Path problems with one constrained resource coordinate.

knowledge_statements.title: Single-Resource Constrained Paths
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shortest-path problem with one additive upper-bounded resource.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a directed graph with source \(s\), sink \(t\), arc costs \(c_a\in\mathbb R\), nonnegative resource consumptions \(r_a\ge0\), and resource limit \(R\ge0\). The single-resource constrained shortest-path problem is \[\min\left\{\sum_{a\in P}c_a: P\text{ is an }s\text{-to-}t\text{ path and }\sum_{a\in P}r_a\le R\right\}.\] Unless elementarity is stated separately, “path” here means a vertex-simple directed path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find a minimum-cost source-to-sink path whose total value of one nonnegative additive resource does not exceed its limit.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,A)\) is finite and directed.
\(r_a\ge0\) for every arc and \(R\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An optimal solution minimizes \(\sum_{a\in P}c_a\) over all \(s\)-to-\(t\) paths satisfying \(\sum_{a\in P}r_a\le R\).

notation.meaning: Single resource consumption of arc a.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The one-resource formulation fits the leaf, but a source is required to validate the consequential convention that path means vertex-simple rather than a resource-feasible walk.

children.title: Multi-Resource Constrained Paths
children.top_down_role: Path problems with several interacting resource coordinates.

knowledge_statements.title: Multi-Resource Constrained Paths
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Shortest-path problem with componentwise bounds on multiple additive resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a finite directed graph with source \(s\), sink \(t\), costs \(c_a\in\mathbb R\), resource vectors \(r_a\in\mathbb R_+^m\), and bounds \(R\in\mathbb R_+^m\). The multi-resource constrained shortest-path problem is \[\min\left\{\sum_{a\in P}c_a: P\text{ is an }s\text{-to-}t\text{ path and }\sum_{a\in P}r_a\le R\right\},\] where the vector inequality is componentwise.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Find a minimum-cost source-to-sink path satisfying simultaneous componentwise upper bounds on several nonnegative additive resources.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,A)\) is finite and directed.
\(r_a\in\mathbb R_+^m\) and \(R\in\mathbb R_+^m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A path \(P\) is resource-feasible exactly when \(\sum_{a\in P}r_a^k\le R^k\) for every \(k\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The componentwise multi-resource formulation is standard and fits the leaf, but it lacks a source and does not state whether paths must be elementary or may contain repetitions.

children.title: Elementary Resource-Constrained Paths
children.top_down_role: Resource-constrained paths with exact nonrepetition requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Elementary Resource-Constrained Paths
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource-constrained shortest paths with explicit vertex nonrepetition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) have source \(s\), sink \(t\), arc costs \(c_a\), resource vectors \(r_a\in\mathbb R_+^m\), and bounds \(R\in\mathbb R_+^m\). An elementary resource-constrained path is an \(s\)-to-\(t\) vertex sequence \(P=(v_0=s,v_1,\ldots,v_k=t)\) such that \((v_{i-1},v_i)\in A\), all vertices \(v_0,\ldots,v_k\) are distinct, and \(\sum_{i=1}^k r_{(v_{i-1},v_i)}\le R\) componentwise. The optimization problem minimizes the corresponding sum of arc costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An elementary resource-constrained path satisfies every resource bound and visits each vertex at most once.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,A)\) is finite and directed.
Arc resources and their bounds are nonnegative vectors.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Feasibility requires both \(v_i\ne v_j\) whenever \(i\ne j\) and \(\sum_{a\in P}r_a\le R\).

notation.meaning: Resource vector consumed by arc a.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition correctly imposes vertex nonrepetition and resource feasibility, and its content kind fits the leaf, but no authoritative source is supplied.

children.title: Cycle-Permitting Resource-Constrained Walks
children.top_down_role: Resource-feasible path models that permit selected revisitations.

knowledge_statements.title: Cycle-Permitting Resource-Constrained Walks
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource-feasible directed walks for which vertex or arc repetition is allowed.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) have source \(s\), sink \(t\), arc costs \(c_a\in\mathbb R\), resources \(r_a\in\mathbb R_+^m\), and bounds \(R\in\mathbb R_+^m\). A cycle-permitting resource-constrained walk is a finite arc sequence \(W=(a_1,\ldots,a_k)\) forming an \(s\)-to-\(t\) directed walk, possibly repeating vertices or arcs, and satisfying \(\sum_{i=1}^k r_{a_i}\le R\) componentwise. Its cost is \(\sum_{i=1}^k c_{a_i}\), with repeated traversals counted with multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: This model allows repeated vertices or arcs while charging every traversal and enforcing total componentwise resource bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,A)\) is finite and directed.
Every resource coordinate is nonnegative and has a finite bound.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A finite \(s\)-to-\(t\) walk \(W\) is feasible exactly when \(\sum_{i=1}^k r_{a_i}\le R\), regardless of repetitions.

notation.meaning: Directed walk with traversals listed in order.
Resource vector consumed per traversal of arc a.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition consistently permits arbitrary finite repetitions, but evidence is needed to confirm whether the terminal container intends unrestricted repetitions or only a narrower class of selected revisitations.

children.title: Robust Resource-Path Extensions
children.top_down_role: Resource-path extensions using set-based uncertainty protection.

knowledge_statements.title: Robust Resource-Path Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact extension for additive resources sharing a represented uncertainty realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a finite acyclic digraph, let \(s,t\in V\), and let \(\mathcal U\) be an uncertainty set. Each arc \(a\) has cost \(c_a\in\mathbb R\) and resource map \(r_a:\mathcal U\to\mathbb R_+^m\). A label for an \(s\)-to-\(v\) path \(P\) stores \((v,c(P),\rho_P)\), where \(c(P)=\sum_{a\in P}c_a\) and \(\rho_P(u)=\sum_{a\in P}r_a(u)\). Initialize \((s,0,0)\). Extending through \(a=(v,w)\) produces \((w,c(P)+c_a,\rho_P+r_a)\). Retain the extension only if \(\sup_{u\in\mathcal U}\rho_{Pa,j}(u)\le b_j\) for every \(j\). After all labels are processed, return a retained label at \(t\) of minimum cost, or infeasibility if none exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Extend each path’s scenario-dependent resource function arc by arc, reject any label violating a resource bound in some scenario, and return the cheapest robust-feasible destination label.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acyclic.
Arc resources are nonnegative and additive for each common realization \(u\in\mathcal U\).
Each displayed supremum can be evaluated exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned label represents a minimum-cost path satisfying \(\rho_{P,j}(u)\le b_j\) for all \(u\in\mathcal U\) and all \(j\).

notation.meaning: scenario-dependent cumulative resource vector of path P

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the robust-extension leaf and the stated exhaustive acyclic labeling procedure is mathematically coherent under common-realization additive resources. No citation or standard-field rationale supports the selected robust uncertainty model, exact supremum oracle, or extension formulation, so source review is required.

children.title: Stochastic Resource-Path Extensions
children.top_down_role: Resource-path extensions using probabilistic uncertainty representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Stochastic Resource-Path Extensions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Chance-constrained extension using exact convolution of independent additive arc resources.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a finite acyclic digraph with source \(s\), destination \(t\), deterministic arc costs \(c_a\), and independent random resource vectors \(R_a\in\mathbb R_+^m\). A label for path \(P\) stores \((v,c(P),\mu_P)\), where \(\mu_P\) is the law of \(S_P=\sum_{a\in P}R_a\). Initialize the source label with \(c=0\) and \(\mu=\delta_0\). Extending through \(a=(v,w)\) sets \(c(Pa)=c(P)+c_a\) and \(\mu_{Pa}=\mu_P*\mu_a\). Retain \(Pa\) only if \(\mathbb P_{\mu_{Pa}}(S_{Pa}\le b)\ge1-\alpha\), with componentwise inequality. Process all retained labels and return a minimum-cost destination label, or infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Convolve the accumulated resource distribution with each independent arc distribution, retain chance-feasible extensions, and select the cheapest destination label.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acyclic.
The vectors \(R_a\) are mutually independent and nonnegative.
Convolution and chance probabilities are computed exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output minimizes deterministic path cost among paths satisfying \(\mathbb P(S_P\le b)\ge1-\alpha\).

notation.meaning: probability law of the cumulative path resource

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role fits the stochastic-extension leaf, but the record supplies no source for the independently distributed arc-resource version. It also does not explicitly introduce the arc law \(\mu_a\) or give domains for \(b\) and \(\alpha\), so the exact sourced formulation must be established before acceptance.

children.title: Uncertainty-Representation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Boundary between deterministic label models and dedicated uncertain-resource treatments.

knowledge_statements.title: Uncertainty-Representation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Marginal resource distributions are insufficient when path and continuation resources are dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a partial path ending at \(v\) with accumulated resource \(X\), where \(\mathbb P(X=0)=\mathbb P(X=1)=1/2\), and one continuation resource \(Y\) having the same Bernoulli marginal. Under one joint model let \(Y=X\); under another let \(Y=1-X\). A label storing only the marginal law of \(X\) is identical in both models, yet for capacity \(b=1\), \(\mathbb P(X+Y\le1)=1/2\) in the first model and \(1\) in the second. Therefore marginal-distribution labels cannot determine extension feasibility when dependence with future resources is unspecified; an exact dynamic program must retain a joint scenario, conditional law, or another extension-sufficient statistic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical marginal labels can yield different completion probabilities under different dependence structures, so exact stochastic extension requires dependence-aware state information.
assumptions_latex: The label records only the marginal distribution of accumulated resource.
Dependence between accumulated and future resources is not represented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: No extension rule based solely on the stored marginal law can be exact for both joint models.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind and the Bernoulli counterexample fit the leaf, and the two stated probabilities are internally correct. The nontrivial extension-sufficiency conclusion has no citation or explicit standard-field rationale, so it remains source-dependent candidate knowledge.

children.title: Label Search Algorithm Family
children.top_down_role: Canonical organizations for selecting, extending, revising, and joining labels.

children.title: Label-Setting Methods
children.top_down_role: Label processing under an ordering that permits permanent settlement.

knowledge_statements.title: Label-Setting Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dijkstra-type permanent settlement on a finite label-state graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=(S,E)\) be a finite directed state graph with source state \(q\), transition lengths \(d_e\ge0\), and target states \(T\subseteq S\). Set \(g(q)=0\), set \(g(x)=+\infty\) otherwise, and mark every state unsettled. Repeatedly select an unsettled state \(x\) of minimum finite \(g(x)\), settle it permanently, and for each transition \(e=(x,y)\) replace \(g(y)\) by \(\min\{g(y),g(x)+d_e\}\), recording a predecessor when improved. Stop when the minimum-key unsettled state is a target, or when no finite key remains. Return its predecessor chain and value, or report that no target is reachable.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly settle the smallest tentative label and relax its outgoing extensions; nonnegative transition costs make every settled value permanent.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is finite.
Every transition length satisfies \(d_e\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each settled value equals the shortest-path value from \(q\), and the returned target has minimum reachable cost.

children.title: Label-Correcting Methods
children.top_down_role: Label processing that permits repeated activation and revision.

knowledge_statements.title: Label-Correcting Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated relaxation with reactivation until no label can improve.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=(S,E)\) be a finite directed state graph with source \(q\), transition lengths \(d_e\in\mathbb R\), and no negative-length cycle reachable from \(q\). Initialize \(g(q)=0\), \(g(x)=+\infty\) for \(x\ne q\), and an active set \(Q=\{q\}\). While \(Q\ne\varnothing\), remove any \(x\in Q\). For every \(e=(x,y)\), if \(g(x)+d_e<g(y)\), set \(g(y)=g(x)+d_e\), record \(x\) as predecessor, and insert or reactivate \(y\) in \(Q\). Stop when \(Q\) is empty and return the finite target labels and their predecessor chains.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Relax labels repeatedly and reactivate every improved state; termination with no active labels yields all reachable shortest-path values when negative cycles are absent.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is finite.
No negative-length cycle is reachable from \(q\).
The activation policy eventually processes every activated state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At termination, \(g(x)\) equals the minimum walk length from \(q\) to every reachable state \(x\).

notation.meaning: active set of states awaiting relaxation
current label value at state x

children.title: Bidirectional Label-Join Interface
children.top_down_role: Forward and backward label generation coupled through a joining interface.

children.title: Forward Label Generation
children.top_down_role: Label exploration proceeding from source-side states.

knowledge_statements.title: Forward Label Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Source-to-meeting-point generation for additive resource-constrained paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a finite acyclic digraph with source \(s\), arc costs \(c_a\), nonnegative resource vectors \(r_a\), and capacity \(b\). Initialize \(L_s=\{(0,0,\varnothing)\}\) and \(L_v=\varnothing\) for \(v\ne s\). Process vertices in topological order. For every label \((C,R,P)\in L_v\) and arc \(a=(v,w)\), form \((C+c_a,R+r_a,P\circ a)\). Insert it into \(L_w\) when \(R+r_a\le b\), then remove any label dominated under an extension-preserving dominance relation. The output is the family \((L_v)_{v\in V}\) of forward labels available for joining or destination selection.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate feasible source-prefix labels in topological order, extend them along outgoing arcs, and discard labels only through extension-preserving dominance.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acyclic.
Resources are nonnegative and additive.
The chosen dominance relation preserves every feasible, no-worse completion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every feasible source-to-\(v\) path, \(L_v\) contains an undominated label capable of representing an equally good completion.

notation.meaning: forward labels ending at vertex v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and forward-generation procedure fit the leaf. The generic dynamic-programming chapter locator does not establish the bidirectional-label setting, the extension-preserving dominance premise, or the stated completion-preservation conclusion; a source with a specific section, theorem, or algorithm locator is required.

children.title: Backward Label Generation
children.top_down_role: Label exploration proceeding from destination-side states.

knowledge_statements.title: Backward Label Generation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Destination-to-meeting-point generation on the reversed graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a finite acyclic digraph with destination \(t\), arc costs \(c_a\), nonnegative resource vectors \(r_a\), and capacity \(b\). Initialize \(B_t=\{(0,0,\varnothing)\}\) and \(B_v=\varnothing\) for \(v\ne t\). Process vertices in reverse topological order. For each \((C,R,P)\in B_w\) and incoming arc \(a=(v,w)\), form \((C+c_a,R+r_a,a\circ P)\). Insert it into \(B_v\) when \(R+r_a\le b\), then remove labels dominated under an extension-preserving backward dominance relation. Output \((B_v)_{v\in V}\) for compatibility tests with forward labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Generate feasible destination-suffix labels backward through incoming arcs and retain the undominated suffixes required for later joins.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acyclic.
Resources are nonnegative and additive.
Backward dominance preserves every feasible, no-worse prefix join.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every feasible \(v\)-to-\(t\) path, \(B_v\) contains an undominated label capable of representing an equally good prefix join.

notation.meaning: backward labels beginning at vertex v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind and reversed-graph suffix generation fit the leaf. The cited generic dynamic-programming chapter does not specifically support backward label generation, backward dominance, or the prefix-join preservation conclusion, so a directly relevant locator is required.

children.title: Label Join Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility structure governing forward–backward label combinations.

knowledge_statements.title: Label Join Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Compatibility predicate for joining elementary forward and backward labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let a forward label at \(v\) represent an elementary path \(P^F:s\leadsto v\) with resource \(R^F\), and let a backward label represent an elementary path \(P^B:v\leadsto t\) with resource \(R^B\). For additive resources and capacity \(b\), define
\[\operatorname{Compat}(P^F,P^B)\iff R^F+R^B\le b\ \text{ and }\ V(P^F)\cap V(P^B)=\{v\}.\]
The inequality is componentwise. When the predicate holds, concatenation at \(v\) is an elementary feasible \(s\)-to-\(t\) path with resource \(R^F+R^B\) and cost \(C^F+C^B\). Conversely, every elementary feasible path split at \(v\) yields a compatible pair under this predicate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two labels may join when their resources fit jointly and their represented paths share no vertex except the meeting vertex.
assumptions_latex: Forward and backward labels retain their visited-vertex sets.
Costs and resources are additive across concatenation.
Feasibility is the componentwise capacity condition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Compatibility is equivalent to elementary feasibility of the concatenated path at the selected meeting vertex.

notation.meaning: forward prefix and backward suffix paths

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind is correct, and the resource and vertex-disjointness predicate is mathematically appropriate for joining elementary paths at a common meeting vertex. No source supports the selected elementary-path variant or its claimed equivalence, so the record requires sourcing.

children.title: Meeting-Point Interfaces
children.top_down_role: State, node, or resource interfaces used to connect directional searches.

knowledge_statements.title: Meeting-Point Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Optimal-path representation through compatible label pairs at allowed meeting vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M\subseteq V\) be meeting vertices intersecting every feasible \(s\)-to-\(t\) path under consideration. For each \(v\in M\), let \(L_v^F\) and \(L_v^B\) be complete forward and backward label sets, and let \(\operatorname{Compat}\) be exact for concatenation. If \(C(\ell)\) denotes label cost, then the optimal path value is
\[z^*=\min_{v\in M}\ \min_{\substack{\ell^F\in L_v^F,\ \ell^B\in L_v^B\\ \operatorname{Compat}(\ell^F,\ell^B)}}\bigl(C(\ell^F)+C(\ell^B)\bigr).\]
An empty inner feasible set has value \(+\infty\). A minimizing pair reconstructs an optimal path by concatenating its represented prefix and suffix at \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The optimum equals the least combined cost of any compatible forward-backward label pair across the permitted meeting vertices.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible path contains a vertex in \(M\).
The label families preserve an optimal prefix and suffix at each relevant meeting vertex.
The compatibility predicate is necessary and sufficient for feasible concatenation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The displayed minimum equals the optimal feasible \(s\)-to-\(t\) path value \(z^*\).

notation.meaning: forward and backward label sets at v

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the meeting-point interface leaf, and the displayed minimum is valid when the label families and compatibility predicate are genuinely complete and exact. Those substantive completeness conditions and the representation formula have no cited support.

children.title: Goal-Bounded Label Search
children.top_down_role: Label selection guided by completion estimates or destination-oriented bounds.

children.title: Goal-Directed Label Selection
children.top_down_role: Label prioritization informed by destination relevance.

knowledge_statements.title: Goal-Directed Label Selection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A-star selection of partial labels using admissible destination estimates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let labels be states of a finite search graph with initial label \(q\), accumulated cost \(g(\ell)\), destination labels \(T\), and completion estimate \(h(\ell)\). Initialize an open set with \(q\), where \(g(q)=0\). Repeatedly remove a label minimizing \(f(\ell)=g(\ell)+h(\ell)\). If it is a destination label, return it. Otherwise generate every feasible extension \(\ell'\), update \(g(\ell')\) when a cheaper representation is found, and insert or reprioritize \(\ell'\). If the open set becomes empty, report infeasibility. With admissible \(h\), the first returned destination is optimal; with consistent \(h\), a permanently selected label need not be reopened.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Select the label with smallest accumulated cost plus an admissible destination estimate; the first destination selected is optimal.
assumptions_latex: The reachable label-state graph is finite.
\(h(\ell)\) never exceeds the cheapest feasible completion cost.
All feasible label extensions are generated.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns a minimum-cost destination label, or correctly reports that none is reachable.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm kind fits goal-directed label selection, but the stated definition of admissibility only requires that \(h\) not exceed completion cost and does not require \(h(t)=0\) for destination labels. Negative destination heuristic values can make the first selected destination suboptimal. Reopening and cycle assumptions also need a precise sourced formulation.

children.title: Completion-Bounded Label Search
children.top_down_role: Search restriction based on estimates of attainable completions.

knowledge_statements.title: Completion-Bounded Label Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe pruning certificate from an incumbent and a valid completion lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a minimization label search with incumbent feasible value \(U\). For a partial label \(\ell\), let \(g(\ell)\) be its accumulated cost and let \(h(\ell)\) be a lower bound on the additional cost of every feasible completion. Then
\[g(\ell)+h(\ell)\ge U\]
is a certificate that no completion of \(\ell\) can improve the incumbent. Hence \(\ell\) and all descendants reachable only through it may be discarded when only an optimal value and one optimizer are required. If no incumbent exists, take \(U=+\infty\). The certificate remains valid after replacing \(U\) by any smaller feasible incumbent value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prune a partial label whenever its accumulated cost plus a valid completion lower bound cannot improve the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is the value of a feasible complete solution.
Every feasible completion of \(\ell\) adds cost at least \(h(\ell)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Discarding \(\ell\) when \(g(\ell)+h(\ell)\ge U\) cannot remove every solution improving \(U\).

notation.meaning: cost accumulated by partial label l

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate kind exactly fits the leaf, and the incumbent-versus-completion-bound pruning condition is internally precise and mathematically correct. The record nevertheless has no citation or explicit standard-field rationale for this nontrivial pruning certificate.

children.title: Destination Heuristics
children.top_down_role: Destination-oriented estimates used to guide label processing.

knowledge_statements.title: Destination Heuristics
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Consistency condition for admissible destination-directed label heuristics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=(S,E)\) be a label-state graph, let \(T\subseteq S\) be destination states, and let transition \((x,y)\in E\) have cost \(d(x,y)\). A destination heuristic \(h:S\to\mathbb R\) is consistent when
\[h(t)=0\quad(t\in T),\qquad h(x)\le d(x,y)+h(y)\quad((x,y)\in E).\]
For every state \(x\) and every finite path from \(x\) to a destination \(t\), repeated application gives \(h(x)\) no larger than that path's cost. Thus \(h\) is an admissible completion lower bound. Moreover, along every transition, the key \(g+h\) is nondecreasing whenever \(g(y)=g(x)+d(x,y)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A heuristic is consistent when it is zero at destinations and obeys a transition triangle inequality; consistency implies admissibility and monotone search keys.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible completion corresponds to a path in \(H\).
Path cost is the sum of transition costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Consistency implies \(h(x)\le d^*(x,T)\) and monotonicity of \(g+h\) along generated paths.

notation.meaning: minimum completion cost from x to a destination

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The condition kind fits the destination-heuristics leaf. The consistency inequalities, admissibility consequence, and monotonicity statement are internally coherent, but no source or explicit standard-field rationale is supplied.

children.title: Bound-Quality Search Regimes
children.top_down_role: Search behavior under differing completion-bound strength.

knowledge_statements.title: Bound-Quality Search Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies destination bounds by their relation to the optimal residual completion cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a label \(L\), let \(g(L)\) be its accumulated cost and let \(h^*(L)\) be the infimum cost of a feasible completion to the destination, with \(h^*(L)=+\infty\) when none exists. A completion estimate \(h(L)\) is exact when \(h(L)=h^*(L)\), admissible when \(h(L)\le h^*(L)\), and inadmissible otherwise. Given incumbent value \(U\), the rule discarding \(L\) whenever \(g(L)+h(L)\ge U\) cannot remove a completion having value below \(U\) in the exact and admissible regimes. No such guarantee follows from inadmissibility alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exact or lower-bounding completion estimates support safe incumbent pruning; overestimating bounds can discard an improving completion.
assumptions_latex: \(U\) is the value of a feasible incumbent solution.
Path cost equals accumulated label cost plus completion cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(h(L)\le h^*(L)\) implies that \(g(L)+h(L)\ge U\) safely certifies that \(L\) cannot improve \(U\).

source_refs.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34

source_witnesses.locator: 2.7 Primal Bounds: Greedy and Local Search p. 34
