knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given current dual prices and a resource limit \(B\), initialize a candidate pool with one or more feasible or partial columns. Until the budget is exhausted, select a candidate by a prescribed heuristic rule, perform chosen feasible extensions or local modifications, evaluate each completed column's reduced cost, and retain the best encountered feasible column. Stop early if an accepted negative-reduced-cost column is found, or stop when \(B\) is exhausted. Return the best improving column found; if none was found, return only “not found,” never the assertion that no improving column exists.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Heuristic pricing searches within a resource budget and may return an improving column, but an unsuccessful run cannot certify that none exists.
assumptions_latex: Every returned column is checked for pricing feasibility.
Reduced cost is evaluated exactly for completed columns.
The search need not explore every feasible column.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex:
\[ar c(
widehat x)<0
implies 
widehat x	ext{ is improving};
qquad 	ext{not found}
ot
gimplies 
min_{xelongs X}ar c(x)
ge0.\]

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and its noncertifying outcome fit Heuristic Pricing, but the conclusion and notation contain corrupted commands, including the reduced-cost symbol, estimator symbol, membership, minimum, and implication. No source supports the proposed generic heuristic-pricing specification or its exact boundary, so a sourced correction is required.

children.title: Truncated Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing terminated under explicit effort, width, depth, or time limits.

knowledge_statements.title: Truncated Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Resource-limited dynamic-programming pricing for a minimization-form restricted master problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given dual vector \(\pi\), tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge 0\), and a pricing state graph whose terminal paths encode columns \(p\in\mathcal P\), assign each path reduced cost \(\bar c_\pi(p)=c_p-\pi^\top a_p\). Initialize the usual dynamic-programming labels and process admissible transitions, but stop after resource budget \(B\) is exhausted or an improving terminal path is found. Output any recovered column \(p\) satisfying \(\bar c_\pi(p)<-\varepsilon\). If all reachable states are processed, additionally output the exact minimum reduced cost; if processing is truncated first, output no optimality certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search the pricing dynamic program only up to a budget, returning any improving column found but no optimality certificate after premature termination.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) is represented exactly by terminal paths of the pricing state graph.
Transition costs sum to \(\bar c_\pi(p)\) on every terminal path.
\(B\) bounds a specified resource such as expanded labels or elapsed iterations.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar c_\pi(p)<-\varepsilon\) certifies improvement, whereas budget exhaustion before complete search does not certify \(\min_{q\in\mathcal P}\bar c_\pi(q)\ge-\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Reduced cost of column p under dual vector pi.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm and its noncertification qualification fit the Truncated Pricing leaf, but no inspectable source supports this specialized pricing policy.

children.title: Improving-Column Discovery
children.top_down_role: Incomplete-search outcomes that identify useful columns without full certification.

knowledge_statements.title: Improving-Column Discovery
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct certificate supplied by an incompletely solved pricing problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a minimization-form master with dual vector \(\pi\) and pricing tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), a column record \((p,a_p,c_p)\) is an improving-column certificate when \(p\in\mathcal P\), its master coefficient vector and cost are correctly evaluated, and \(c_p-\pi^\top a_p< -\varepsilon\). The certificate is verified by checking pricing feasibility and the displayed scalar inequality. Its validity requires neither global minimization of reduced cost nor exhaustion of the dynamic-programming state space; it establishes only the existence of a column capable of violating the current reduced-cost optimality condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A feasible column with verifiably negative reduced cost certifies improvement even when the pricing search is incomplete.
assumptions_latex: The restricted master is written in minimization form with dual vector \(\pi\).
The pricing feasibility test for \(p\in\mathcal P\) is exact.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p\in\mathcal P\) and \(c_p-\pi^\top a_p< -\varepsilon\) constitute a verifiable improving-column certificate.

notation.meaning: Master coefficient vector of column p.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The certificate is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but the record supplies no source for the column-generation interpretation and verification conditions.

children.title: Noncertification Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Limits on oracle conclusions after incomplete pricing exploration.

knowledge_statements.title: Noncertification Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical limitation of incomplete reduced-cost search.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(S\subsetneq\mathcal P\) be the columns examined by an incomplete pricing call. Observing \(\bar c_\pi(p)\ge-\varepsilon\) for every \(p\in S\) does not imply \(\min_{p\in\mathcal P}\bar c_\pi(p)\ge-\varepsilon\). Indeed, an unexamined column \(q\in\mathcal P\setminus S\) may satisfy \(\bar c_\pi(q)<-\varepsilon\). Consequently, failure of truncated or heuristic pricing to find an improving column cannot certify restricted-master optimality for the full master unless an independently valid lower bound or exhaustive exact oracle proves the global reduced-cost inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure on a proper subset of columns cannot certify that no improving column exists in the full pricing set.
assumptions_latex: \(S\subsetneq\mathcal P\) is the set actually examined.
No valid global lower bound on unexamined reduced costs is available.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\forall p\in S:\bar c_\pi(p)\ge-\varepsilon\not\Rightarrow\min_{p\in\mathcal P}\bar c_\pi(p)\ge-\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Reduced-cost function at the current dual vector.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure boundary is logically correct and appropriately classified, but it has no cited source or inspectable locator.

children.title: Diversified Multi-Column Pricing
children.top_down_role: Retention of several improving paths, labels, or patterns from one oracle invocation.

children.title: Multiple-Column Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing calls retaining several improving columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Multiple-Column Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Repeated exact pricing with exclusions to obtain distinct improving columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given \(K\in\mathbb N\), dual vector \(\pi\), and tolerance \(\varepsilon\ge0\), initialize \(Q=\varnothing\). For \(j=1,\ldots,K\), solve the pricing problem exactly over \(\mathcal P\setminus Q\). If this set is empty, stop. Otherwise obtain a minimizer \(p_j\). If \(\bar c_\pi(p_j)<-\varepsilon\), set \(Q\leftarrow Q\cup\{p_j\}\); otherwise stop. Output \(Q\). If a solve proves that its feasible set is empty or that its minimum is at least \(-\varepsilon\), then no additional distinct improving column exists outside \(Q\); otherwise the procedure returns at most \(K\) pairwise distinct improving columns.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly solve exact pricing while excluding previously selected columns, stopping after K distinct improving columns, an empty remaining set, or a certified minimum that is not improving.
assumptions_latex: The pricing oracle can enforce finite column exclusions exactly and report an empty feasible set.
Every nonempty pricing subproblem encountered attains its minimum.
Column identity is decidable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|Q|\le K\), the elements of \(Q\) are distinct, and \(\bar c_\pi(p)<-\varepsilon\) for every \(p\in Q\).

children.title: Diversified Pricing
children.top_down_role: Pricing that favors structural variation among retained columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Diversified Pricing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Greedy selection balancing normalized reduced-cost improvement and dissimilarity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\subseteq\mathcal P\) be a nonempty finite pool with \(\bar c_\pi(p)<-\varepsilon\) for all \(p\in C\). Let \(r:C\to[0,1]\) be a normalized improvement score, let \(d:C\times C\to[0,1]\) be a dissimilarity, and choose \(K\in\mathbb N\) with \(K\ge1\) and \(\alpha\in[0,1]\). Initialize \(Q\) with a maximizer of \(r\) over \(C\). While \(|Q|<\min\{K,|C|\}\), add a maximizer over \(p\in C\setminus Q\) of \(\alpha r(p)+(1-\alpha)\min_{q\in Q}d(p,q)\). Output \(Q\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: From a nonempty pool of improving columns, greedily select up to K columns using normalized improvement and dissimilarity scores.
assumptions_latex: \(C\) is finite, nonempty, and contains only improving columns.
The scores \(r\) and \(d\) are computable and take values in \([0,1]\).
Ties are resolved by a fixed rule.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Q\subseteq C\), \(|Q|=\min\{K,|C|\}\), and every \(p\in Q\) satisfies \(\bar c_\pi(p)<-\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Normalized reduced-cost improvement score of column p.
Weight on the normalized improvement score.

children.title: Column-Pool Retention
children.top_down_role: Policies governing which improving candidates survive an oracle call.

knowledge_statements.title: Column-Pool Retention
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded retention of reusable columns across master iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At master iteration \(t\), take the previous pool \(R_{t-1}\), newly generated columns \(G_t\), current dual vector \(\pi_t\), and capacity \(H\). Remove infeasible columns and merge columns having identical master representations. Recompute \(\bar c_{\pi_t}(p)\) for every survivor, rank survivors by a fixed retention score \(s_t(p)\), and let \(R_t\) be the first \(H\) columns, or all survivors if fewer exist. Return improving members of \(R_t\) for possible insertion. Pool absence never certifies nonexistence of improving columns, so exact pricing remains necessary whenever certification is required.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Maintain a bounded, deduplicated pool of feasible columns, rescored under current duals, without treating pool failure as pricing certification.
assumptions_latex: Column feasibility and master representation can be checked exactly.
The retention score \(s_t\) defines a deterministic total preorder.
\(H\in\mathbb N\) is the pool capacity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(|R_t|\le H\), and every retained column is feasible and has a uniquely represented master column within \(R_t\).

children.title: Duplicate-Column Suppression
children.top_down_role: Controls limiting equivalent or near-redundant pricing outputs.

knowledge_statements.title: Duplicate-Column Suppression
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe suppression based on equality of complete master representations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate each generated object \(p\in\mathcal P\) with a canonical signature \(\sigma(p)\). Duplicate suppression is master-safe when \(\sigma(p)=\sigma(q)\) implies \((a_p,c_p)=(a_q,c_q)\), including every coefficient used by active master rows and cuts. Given the accepted-signature set \(D\), accept \(p\) exactly when \(\sigma(p)\notin D\), then update \(D\leftarrow D\cup\{\sigma(p)\}\). Under the implication above, rejection removes only a column identical in the current master formulation to one already accepted; a signature omitting an active coefficient does not satisfy this safety condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reject repeated canonical signatures only when signature equality guarantees equality of every objective and active master coefficient.
assumptions_latex: Each column has a computable canonical signature.
All active master-row and cut coefficients are included in the represented data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\sigma(p)\in D\) may be rejected safely provided \(\sigma(p)=\sigma(q)\Rightarrow(a_p,c_p)=(a_q,c_q)\).

notation.meaning: Complete current master representation of column p.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The safety condition correctly requires equality of the complete active master representation and fits the leaf, but no source supports the stated suppression criterion.

children.title: Adaptive Pricing Effort
children.top_down_role: Variation of state-space effort with master progress and certification needs.

knowledge_statements.title: Adaptive Pricing Effort
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Escalation of pricing effort as improvement becomes harder or certification becomes necessary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(B_1\le B_2\le\cdots\le B_m\) be pricing-search budgets, with level \(m\) denoting exhaustive exact solution. At a master iteration, begin at a prescribed level and increase the level whenever a call finds no improving column but termination still requires pricing certification. A discovered column \(p\) with \(\bar c_\pi(p)<-\varepsilon\) may be returned immediately. The master may declare absence of improving columns only after level \(m\), or another call furnishing a valid global lower bound, proves \(\min_{p\in\mathcal P}\bar c_\pi(p)\ge-\varepsilon\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Use cheap pricing first, escalate after unsuccessful calls, and require an exact bound before declaring that no improving column exists.
assumptions_latex: The budgets satisfy \(B_1\le\cdots\le B_m\).
Level \(m\) solves the pricing problem exactly.
The master distinguishes improvement discovery from optimality certification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination for lack of improving columns is permitted only with a valid proof of \(\min_{p\in\mathcal P}\bar c_\pi(p)\ge-\varepsilon\).

notation.meaning: Pricing effort budget at level j.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle matches adaptive pricing effort and correctly separates discovery from certification, but the staged escalation policy has no supporting citation.

children.title: Pricing-Oracle Adaptation
children.top_down_role: State-model changes required by branching decisions, master cuts, and repeated oracle calls.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Sections 11.4–11.7: Branch-and-price variants and computational issues

children.title: Branching-Induced Transition Restrictions
children.top_down_role: Branching decisions implemented through allowed or forbidden pricing transitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching-Induced Transition Restrictions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact implementation of local branching rules by deleting pricing transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a pricing state graph whose source-to-terminal paths encode columns, and let a branch node permit exactly the path set \(\mathcal Q\). If there exists \(E_b\subseteq E\) such that a source-to-terminal path belongs to \(\mathcal Q\) exactly when every one of its edges lies in \(E_b\), then the node pricing problem is represented by the restricted graph \(G_b=(V,E_b)\) with unchanged transition costs. Dynamic programming on \(G_b\) therefore optimizes over precisely the branch-feasible columns; branch rules lacking such an edge-local characterization require additional state or another formulation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Delete transitions when branch feasibility is exactly characterized by using only allowed edges; otherwise transition restriction alone is insufficient.
assumptions_latex: Source-to-terminal paths of \(G\) encode the original pricing columns exactly.
Branch feasibility has the stated edge-local characterization.
The restricted graph remains within the dynamic program's solvable graph class.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Paths}(G_b)=\mathcal Q\), so optimization on \(G_b\) is exact for the branch-node pricing set.

notation.meaning: Transitions allowed by the branch decision.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The edge-local representation is precise and fits the transition-restriction topic, but branch-and-price or dynamic-programming source support is absent.

children.title: Branching-Induced State Augmentation
children.top_down_role: Additional pricing resources or memory required by branch decisions.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching-Induced State Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-state construction for finite-memory branch feasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) encode pricing paths and let \(M=(S,s_0,\delta,F)\) be a deterministic finite-memory machine that accepts exactly the paths satisfying a branch decision. Form product states \((v,s)\in V\times S\); for each edge \(e=(v,w)\), include \((v,s)\to(w,\delta(s,e))\) with the original edge cost. A product path is terminal only when its memory component lies in \(F\). Projection onto \(G\) gives a cost-preserving bijection between accepted product paths and branch-feasible original paths, so dynamic programming on the product graph solves the adapted pricing problem exactly.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Combine each pricing state with finite branch memory; accepting product paths then represent exactly the branch-feasible columns.
assumptions_latex: The original pricing problem has an exact path representation on \(G\).
A deterministic finite-memory machine recognizes branch-feasible paths.
The product state space is computationally admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{Paths}_{\mathrm{term}}(G\times M)\) projects bijectively and cost-preservingly onto the branch-feasible paths of \(G\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The finite-memory product construction is mathematically coherent and fits state augmentation, but the specialized branch-pricing claim lacks an inspectable source.

children.title: Master-Cut State Augmentation
children.top_down_role: Pricing-state information required to compute coefficients of master-side cuts.

knowledge_statements.title: Master-Cut State Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-state computation of path-dependent master-cut coefficients.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose a master cut requires coefficient \(\gamma(p)\) for each pricing path \(p=(e_1,\ldots,e_k)\), and a finite state set \(Z\), initial state \(z_0\), update \(z_i=U(z_{i-1},e_i)\), and terminal map \(h\) satisfy \(\gamma(p)=h(z_k)\). Augment each pricing state \(v\) to \((v,z)\) and each edge \(e=(v,w)\) to \((v,z)\to(w,U(z,e))\). Terminal product states then determine the exact cut coefficient through \(h(z)\), allowing reduced costs containing the cut dual multiplier to be evaluated within the dynamic program.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Track finite path memory sufficient to compute each generated column's coefficient in an active master cut.
assumptions_latex: Every pricing column is represented by a finite path.
The cut coefficient admits the stated finite-state recursion.
The cut's dual contribution is computable from the terminal augmented state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\gamma(p)=h(z_k)\) is exactly recoverable from the terminal state of the augmented pricing path.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly describes finite-state recovery of cut coefficients, but no source supports its application to master-cut pricing augmentation.

children.title: Cross-Context Pricing-State Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of state graphs, bounds, and labels across related pricing calls.

children.title: Master-Iteration State Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of pricing structures across successive master-problem iterations.

knowledge_statements.title: Master-Iteration State Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reuse of unchanged pricing topology while recomputing dual-dependent values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At master iteration \(t+1\), suppose the pricing state graph, feasibility transitions, and topological order are unchanged from iteration \(t\), while transition weights change from \(w_t\) to \(w_{t+1}\) because the dual vector changes. Retain the graph, predecessor lists, order, and dual-independent transition data; invalidate all dual-dependent labels and bounds; recompute \(w_{t+1}\); then run the dynamic-programming recurrence in the retained order and recover a minimizing terminal path. Reuse a former numeric label or pruning bound only if it is separately proved valid under \(w_{t+1}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse unchanged state-graph structure across master iterations, but recompute every dual-dependent weight, label, and uncertified bound.
assumptions_latex: The feasible pricing paths and graph topology do not change between the two iterations.
The new transition weights can be recomputed from current dual data.
The dynamic-programming recurrence is exact in the retained order.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Recomputation with \(w_{t+1}\) yields the same optimum as a fresh dynamic-programming solve on the unchanged graph.

notation.meaning: Transition weights at master iteration t.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The reuse algorithm appropriately invalidates dual-dependent quantities and fits the leaf, but its exactness and stale-bound restrictions are unsupported by a cited source.

children.title: Search-Node State Reuse
children.top_down_role: Reuse of pricing structures across related branch-and-bound nodes.

knowledge_statements.title: Search-Node State Reuse
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe transfer of dynamic-programming labels between branch-and-bound search nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let search nodes \(u\) and \(v\) induce feasible partial-state sets \(F_u\) and \(F_v\), and let \(L_u(s)\) store a label for state \(s\). Initialize the pricing dynamic program at \(v\) with precisely the cached labels satisfying \(s\in F_v\). Recompute every objective-dependent key and discard each cached dominance decision unless its feasibility and dominance predicates remain valid at \(v\). Continue the ordinary label extension and dominance procedure under the data of \(v\), and output only complete labels feasible for \(v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reuse only labels feasible at the new search node, recompute objective-dependent values, and revalidate dominance before continuing the pricing dynamic program.
assumptions_latex: \(F_u\) and \(F_v\) use the same state encoding and transition semantics.
Feasibility at node \(v\) is decidable for every cached state.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The initialized search contains no state known to violate \(F_v\), and its returned complete labels are feasible at node \(v\).

notation.meaning: partial states feasible at search node v
cached label associated with state s at node u

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the leaf, but the cited general dynamic-programming and branch-and-bound sections do not directly support cross-node label transfer, dominance revalidation, or the assumption that state feasibility also certifies the cached partial path.

children.title: Reusable State Graphs
children.top_down_role: Persistent state-network structures shared by related pricing calls.

knowledge_statements.title: Reusable State Graphs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Context-independent graph representation supporting repeated pricing solves.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A reusable state graph is a directed acyclic graph \(G=(V,E)\) with source \(r\), terminal set \(T\), context-independent transitions \(E\), and context-dependent arc feasibility and weight maps \(a_\theta:E\to\{0,1\}\) and \(w_\theta:E\to\mathbb R\). For context \(\theta\), feasible pricing objects are represented by \(r\)-to-\(T\) paths using only arcs \(e\) with \(a_\theta(e)=1\), and each path \(P\) has value \(\sum_{e\in P}w_\theta(e)\). Reuse retains \(G\) while reevaluating \(a_\theta\), \(w_\theta\), and all context-dependent labels.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed acyclic state graph can serve many pricing contexts when arc feasibility, weights, and dependent labels are reevaluated for each context.
assumptions_latex: Every feasible pricing object has at least one source-to-terminal path representation in \(G\).
The graph topology and transition meanings do not depend on \(\theta\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For each context \(\theta\), pricing reduces to an admissible shortest-path computation on the retained graph \(G\).

notation.meaning: pricing context, including duals and search-node restrictions
context-dependent arc admissibility and weight maps

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the leaf, but the stated assumptions guarantee only that feasible objects have paths, not that every admissible source-to-terminal path represents a feasible object. The claimed shortest-path reduction and cross-context reuse require direct support and a converse representation condition.

children.title: Stale-Bound Safety
children.top_down_role: Validity limits for reusing bounds after dual or restriction changes.

knowledge_statements.title: Stale-Bound Safety
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Validity condition for pruning with a bound computed in an earlier pricing context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Q_\theta(s)\) be the minimum completion value from state \(s\) in pricing context \(\theta\). A cached value \(B_{\theta_0}(s)\) may be used at a new context \(\theta_1\) to prune \(s\) against incumbent value \(U_{\theta_1}\) only if \(B_{\theta_0}(s)\le Q_{\theta_1}(s)\) has been established. Under minimization, pruning is then permitted when \(B_{\theta_0}(s)\ge U_{\theta_1}\). Without cross-context validity, the bound must be recomputed or ignored, irrespective of its validity under \(\theta_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cached lower bound may prune in a new context only after it is shown to remain a lower bound for that context.
assumptions_latex: Pricing is a minimization problem.
\(U_{\theta_1}\) is the value of a feasible completion or the applicable pruning threshold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The conjunction \(B_{\theta_0}(s)\le Q_{\theta_1}(s)\) and \(B_{\theta_0}(s)\ge U_{\theta_1}\) safely excludes an improving completion from \(s\).

notation.meaning: optimal completion value from state s in context theta
cached lower bound from the old context

children.title: Pricing-Oracle Failure Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Conditions that undermine pricing certification or manageable state-space behavior.

children.title: Incomplete-Pricing Noncertification
children.top_down_role: Failure of a partial pricing search to certify absence of improving columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Incomplete-Pricing Noncertification
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical failure of optimality certification after searching only part of the pricing domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal P\) be the full column set, \(S\subsetneq\mathcal P\) the subset examined by an incomplete pricing procedure, and \(\bar c_\pi(p)\) the reduced cost at dual vector \(\pi\). The condition \(\min_{p\in S}\bar c_\pi(p)\ge0\) does not imply \(\min_{p\in\mathcal P}\bar c_\pi(p)\ge0\). Indeed, for \(\mathcal P=\{p_1,p_2\}\), \(S=\{p_1\}\), \(\bar c_\pi(p_1)=0\), and \(\bar c_\pi(p_2)=-1\), the partial search finds no improving column although one exists. Certification requires an exact pricing optimum or a valid global lower bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Failure to find a negative-reduced-cost column in a searched subset does not certify that none exists in the full pricing domain.
assumptions_latex: A column is improving exactly when its reduced cost is negative.
The searched set \(S\) need not equal the full set \(\mathcal P\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Partial-search nonimprovement alone is not a certificate that \(\min_{p\in\mathcal P}\bar c_\pi(p)\ge0\).

notation.meaning: reduced cost of column p at dual vector pi

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The counterexample and noncertification conclusion are correct and fit the failure-boundary leaf, but the record supplies no source for the column-generation certification claim.

children.title: Dual-Frontier Instability Coupling
children.top_down_role: Rapidly changing dual information causing unstable pricing frontiers.

children.title: Dual Instability
children.top_down_role: Rapid variation in dual-adjusted pricing information.

knowledge_statements.title: Dual Instability
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantitative dual oscillation across successive restricted-master iterations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For restricted-master dual vectors \(\pi^0,\pi^1,\ldots\in\mathbb R^m\), define the step variation \(D_k=\lVert\pi^{k+1}-\pi^k\rVert\). Relative to tolerances \(\delta>0\) and window length \(q\ge2\), the sequence is dual-unstable at iteration \(k\) when \(D_j>\delta\) for at least two indices \(j\in\{k-q+1,\ldots,k\}\), or when successive differences reverse direction, \(\langle\pi^{j+1}-\pi^j,\pi^j-\pi^{j-1}\rangle<0\), within that window. The definition is norm- and tolerance-dependent and concerns iteration behavior, not dual infeasibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dual instability is persistent large movement or directional reversal of restricted-master dual vectors over a specified iteration window.
assumptions_latex: All dual vectors use a common constraint ordering and scaling.
A norm, tolerance \(\delta\), and window length \(q\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The predicates on \(D_j\) and successive differences provide an operational dual-instability classification.

notation.meaning: restricted-master dual vector at iteration k
norm of the dual step from iteration k to k+1

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed threshold-and-window predicate is an operational convention rather than a canonical definition of dual instability. It has no source, and the admissible iteration range needed to make the window indices valid is not specified.

children.title: Label Churn
children.top_down_role: Repeated turnover in competitive pricing labels or frontiers.

knowledge_statements.title: Label Churn
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Turnover of retained dynamic-programming labels after a pricing-context change.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L_k(s)\) be the set of nondominated labels retained at state \(s\) during pricing iteration \(k\). For finite aggregate label sets \(L_k=\bigcup_s L_k(s)\), define label churn by \[C_k=\frac{|L_{k+1}\mathbin{\triangle}L_k|}{|L_{k+1}\cup L_k|},\] with \(C_k=0\) when both sets are empty. Thus \(0\le C_k\le1\); value zero means identical retained-label sets, while value one means complete turnover. Label identity must be based on context-independent state and resource data rather than the context-dependent reduced-cost key.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Label churn is the normalized symmetric-difference turnover of nondominated label sets between consecutive pricing iterations.
assumptions_latex: Each aggregate retained-label set is finite.
Labels have a context-independent identity suitable for cross-iteration comparison.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The statistic \(C_k\in[0,1]\) quantifies retained-label turnover between iterations \(k\) and \(k+1\).

notation.meaning: nondominated labels retained at state s in iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The normalized symmetric-difference statistic is internally coherent and fits the title, but presenting it as the definition of label churn requires a source establishing this metric and its cross-context label-identity convention.

children.title: Frontier Volatility
children.top_down_role: Pricing regimes with unstable sets of nondominated labels.

knowledge_statements.title: Frontier Volatility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Turnover of the nondominated frontier under changing dual prices or restrictions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_k\) denote the finite set of context-independent label identities on the nondominated frontier after pricing iteration \(k\). Define frontier volatility by \[V_k=1-\frac{|F_k\cap F_{k+1}|}{|F_k\cup F_{k+1}|},\] with \(V_k=0\) when both frontiers are empty. Then \(0\le V_k\le1\); \(V_k=0\) means the frontier is unchanged and \(V_k=1\) means the two nonempty frontiers are disjoint. The statistic measures set turnover and does not by itself measure the magnitude of objective-value changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Frontier volatility is the Jaccard distance between nondominated label frontiers in consecutive pricing contexts.
assumptions_latex: The frontiers \(F_k\) and \(F_{k+1}\) are finite.
Frontier elements have context-independent identities.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The value \(V_k\in[0,1]\) measures nondominated-frontier turnover across consecutive contexts.

notation.meaning: nondominated frontier at pricing iteration k

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Jaccard-distance formula is mathematically correct, but no source establishes it as the relevant definition of frontier volatility or supports the required context-independent frontier identity convention.

children.title: Stabilization Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Interfaces through which stabilized master information influences pricing.

knowledge_statements.title: Stabilization Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interface between a dual-stabilized master and a dynamic-programming pricing oracle.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: At iteration \(k\), the master supplies a pricing vector \(\tilde\pi^k\), a certification vector \(\pi^k\), and current search-node restrictions. The pricing oracle first evaluates arc weights and searches using \(\tilde\pi^k\), returning candidate columns and valid search bounds tagged with their generating vector. Before termination is declared, it reevaluates candidates and solves or globally bounds the full pricing problem under \(\pi^k\). It may report certification only when the resulting global lower bound on reduced cost is nonnegative; bounds generated solely under \(\tilde\pi^k\) cannot certify the vector \(\pi^k\) without a proved transfer inequality.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stabilization interface separates exploratory pricing duals from certification duals and requires exact or globally bounded repricing before termination.
assumptions_latex: Reduced costs can be evaluated under both supplied dual vectors.
The oracle can produce an exact optimum or a valid global lower bound for certification.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A nonnegative global pricing bound under \(\pi^k\) certifies absence of a negative-reduced-cost column for \(\pi^k\).

notation.meaning: stabilized vector used for exploratory pricing
dual vector for which pricing certification is required

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic interface fits the leaf and correctly separates exploratory pricing from certification, but the two-vector protocol, tagged bounds, and required repricing behavior need a direct stabilized-column-generation source.

children.title: Master-Restriction State-Explosion Boundary
children.top_down_role: Growth in pricing-state memory caused by accumulated master-side restrictions.

children.title: Branching-Induced State Explosion
children.top_down_role: Pricing-state growth caused by accumulated branching restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Branching-Induced State Explosion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential dynamic-programming state growth caused by independent branching memories.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a pricing dynamic program augmented to enforce \(b\) independent binary branching conditions. Suppose two partial paths reaching the same original state may be extended differently whenever their satisfaction vectors \(z\in\{0,1\}^b\) differ. Any exact Markovian state representation must then distinguish all reachable vectors \(z\). If every vector is reachable at some layer, that layer contains at least \(2^b\) augmented states per original state. Hence branching constraints that cannot be encoded by a bounded-size aggregate destroy polynomial state growth when \(b\) is part of the input.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent branching conditions can require a distinct dynamic-programming state for every binary satisfaction pattern, producing exponential growth in the branch count.
assumptions_latex: The \(b\) branching conditions have independently reachable satisfaction patterns.
Different patterns can admit different future extensions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The augmented state count is at least \(2^b\) per affected original state in the stated family.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional distinguishability argument fits the failure-boundary leaf, but the cited general branch-and-bound section does not directly substantiate the asserted exact-state lower bound for branching memories.

children.title: Cut-Induced State Explosion
children.top_down_role: Pricing-state growth caused by master-cut information.

knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Induced State Explosion
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exponential state growth from exact tracking of independent cut contributions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(c\) added master cuts whose column coefficients must be computed during pricing. Suppose each partial path has a binary contribution vector \(y\in\{0,1\}^c\), every vector is reachable, and for each pair of distinct vectors some continuation has feasibility or reduced cost depending on their difference. Then no exact Markovian pricing dynamic program may merge those two vectors. Consequently an affected layer requires at least \(2^c\) augmented states per original state. Cuts whose coefficients admit no lower-dimensional sufficient statistic therefore cause exponential state growth when their number is unbounded.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent cut-contribution patterns can force exact pricing to retain exponentially many augmented states.
assumptions_latex: All \(2^c\) binary cut-contribution vectors are reachable.
Distinct contribution vectors are distinguishable by some feasible continuation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The exact augmented dynamic program requires at least \(2^c\) states per affected original state in this family.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record states a specialized continuation-distinguishability lower bound for cut-coefficient memories. The cited general branch-and-cut section is insufficiently direct to support that exact claim.

children.title: Combined-Restriction Accumulation
children.top_down_role: State growth arising from simultaneous branch-side and cut-side restrictions.

knowledge_statements.title: Combined-Restriction Accumulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative state growth when independent branching and cut memories accumulate.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an original dynamic-programming state be augmented by a branching-memory component \(z\in Z\) and a cut-memory component \(y\in Y\). If every pair \((z,y)\in Z\times Y\) is reachable and any two distinct pairs are distinguishable by some continuation, an exact Markovian representation requires at least \(|Z||Y|\) augmented states per affected original state. In particular, \(b\) independent binary branching memories and \(c\) independent binary cut memories yield \(|Z||Y|=2^{b+c}\). Thus restrictions accumulate multiplicatively unless a smaller joint sufficient statistic preserves feasibility and continuation costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Independent branching and cut memories multiply the required augmented-state count; binary memories yield up to exponential growth in their combined number.
assumptions_latex: Every pair in \(Z\times Y\) is reachable.
Distinct pairs have different feasible-continuation sets or continuation costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At least \(|Z||Y|\) augmented states are necessary, equaling \(2^{b+c}\) for independent binary components.

notation.meaning: numbers of binary branching and cut memories

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product-count conclusion follows under the strong reachability and distinguishability assumptions and fits the leaf, but the cited source does not directly support this multiplicative exact-state lower bound.

children.title: State-Augmentation Scalability Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits on pricing viability as restriction memory expands.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Augmentation Scalability Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Product-cardinality boundary for explicit augmented-state dynamic programming.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a base dynamic program have \(N\) states and \(M\) transitions, and augment each state by components with finite domains \(R_1,\ldots,R_q\). Explicit enumeration has at most \(N\prod_{j=1}^q|R_j|\) states and, under bounded transition branching, time \(O\!\left(M\prod_{j=1}^q|R_j|\right)\). It is polynomial in the encoded input size only when the product of domain cardinalities is polynomially bounded. If \(q\) independent binary components are necessary and jointly reachable, the state and time factors are at least \(2^q\), marking the scalability boundary of explicit augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Explicit state augmentation is polynomial only while the product of added component-domain sizes remains polynomially bounded; independent binary components create an exponential boundary.
assumptions_latex: All augmented components are explicitly enumerated.
Transition processing per augmented transition is polynomial-time.
The lower-bound case has jointly reachable, continuation-distinguishable component values.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The explicit resource bounds scale by \(\prod_{j=1}^q|R_j|\), and by at least \(2^q\) for necessary independent binary components.

notation.meaning: base numbers of states and transitions
domain of augmented state component j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The product-cardinality intuition fits the complexity-bound leaf, but the time bound requires an explicit transition-lifting model, and the polynomial-only-if statement requires full Cartesian enumeration or comparable reachability assumptions. The cited general dynamic-programming chapter does not directly support these claims.

children.title: DP-Derived Solver Representation Family
children.top_down_role: Structures through which a dynamic program becomes an extended formulation, decision diagram, bound generator, or structured solver component.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Arc Flow Formulations Based on Dynamic Programming: Theoretical Foundations and Applications

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Arc Flow Formulations Based on Dynamic Programming: Theoretical Foundations and Applications

children.title: State-Network Flow Formulations
children.top_down_role: Explicit flow formulations derived from dynamic-programming state networks.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Arc Flow Formulations Based on Dynamic Programming: Theoretical Foundations and Applications
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Sections 2–5: Foundations, Dantzig–Wolfe relation, state-space relaxation, and dual perspective
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Arc Flow Formulations Based on Dynamic Programming: Theoretical Foundations and Applications

children.title: Exact DP Network Formulations
children.top_down_role: State networks whose terminal paths represent feasible integer decisions exactly.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact DP Network Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact finite acyclic state-network formulation of an integer feasible set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) be finite and let \(G=(V,A)\) be a finite acyclic multigraph with source \(s\), sink \(t\), and arc increments \(d_a\in\mathbb Z^n\). The network is exact for \(X\) when
\[
X=\left\{\sum_{a\in P}d_a:P\text{ is an }s\text{-}t\text{ path in }G\right\}.
\]
Writing \(B\) for the node-arc incidence matrix and \(b=e_s-e_t\), an exact extended formulation is
\[
Bf=b,\qquad f\geq0,\qquad x=\sum_{a\in A}d_af_a.
\]
Every extreme feasible flow is a path incidence vector, so projection onto \(x\) gives \(\operatorname{conv}(X)\); imposing \(f\in\mathbb Z^A\) represents individual feasible integer decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact acyclic DP network has precisely the feasible integer decisions as terminal-path labels, and its unit-flow formulation projects to their convex hull.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq\mathbb Z^n\) is finite.
\(G\) is finite, acyclic, and has distinguished source \(s\) and sink \(t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_x\{(x,f):Bf=e_s-e_t,\ f\geq0,\ x=\sum_a d_af_a\}=\operatorname{conv}(X)\).

notation.meaning: integer decision increment carried by arc a
node-arc incidence matrix using the outflow-minus-inflow convention

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the exact-network container and is mathematically plausible under the stated finite acyclic assumptions, but no citation or inspectable locator supports the exact-formulation and convex-hull claims.

children.title: Arc-Flow Pattern Formulations
children.top_down_role: Aggregated state-network flow models for packing, cutting, scheduling, and routing structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Arc-Flow Pattern Formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Aggregated arc-flow representation of path-indexed feasible patterns.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let each source-to-sink path \(P\) of an acyclic network encode a feasible pattern with resource vector \(q(P)=\sum_{a\in P}q_a\) and additive cost \(c(P)=\sum_{a\in P}c_a\). For an integer number \(m\) of selected patterns, path variables \(y_P\in\mathbb Z_+\) may be replaced by arc variables
\[
f_a=\sum_{P\ni a}y_P,
\]
which satisfy \(Bf=m(e_s-e_t)\) and \(f\in\mathbb Z_+^A\). Any pattern-level aggregate condition \(\sum_P q(P)y_P\mathrel{\unrhd}r\) becomes \(\sum_a q_af_a\mathrel{\unrhd}r\), while the objective becomes \(\sum_a c_af_a\). Thus the arc model is an aggregated formulation of the same pattern multiset problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Path-indexed patterns can be aggregated into integer arc flows when pattern resources and costs are additive along network paths.
assumptions_latex: The network is finite and acyclic.
Every feasible pattern is represented by a source-to-sink path, with additive resources and cost.
\(\unrhd\) is a fixed componentwise relation such as \(\geq\), \(=\), or \(\leq\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f_a=\sum_{P\ni a}y_P\) preserves total pattern count, aggregate resources, and additive objective value.

notation.meaning: number of selected patterns or flow value

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits the arc-flow pattern container, and additivity plus acyclicity supports the stated aggregation. No citation or inspectable locator is supplied for the pattern-to-arc-flow equivalence.

children.title: Path-Arc Flow Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural relationship between path-based decomposition models and explicit arc-flow models.

children.title: Path-Flow Representations
children.top_down_role: Decomposition representations whose variables correspond to complete state-network paths.

assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acyclic.
Arc labels and costs are additive along paths.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(x=\sum_{P\in\mathcal P}d(P)z_P\) and \(C=\sum_{P\in\mathcal P}c(P)z_P\) represent the weighted path collection.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Nonnegative flow represented directly by source-to-sink path weights.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a finite acyclic directed graph with source \(s\), sink \(t\), and source-to-sink path set \(\mathcal P\). A path-flow representation of value \(\rho\geq0\) is a vector \(z\in\mathbb R_+^{\mathcal P}\) satisfying
\[
\sum_{P\in\mathcal P}z_P=\rho.
\]
If path \(P\) carries label \(d(P)=\sum_{a\in P}d_a\) and cost \(c(P)=\sum_{a\in P}c_a\), then the represented aggregate decision and cost are
\[
x=\sum_{P\in\mathcal P}d(P)z_P,
\qquad
C=\sum_{P\in\mathcal P}c(P)z_P.
\]
Integral \(z\) represents a multiset of terminal paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A path-flow assigns nonnegative weights to terminal paths; their sum is the flow value and their weighted labels give the aggregate decision.
knowledge_statements.title: Path-Flow Representations

children.title: Arc-Flow Representations
children.top_down_role: Explicit network representations whose variables correspond to state transitions.

knowledge_statements.title: Arc-Flow Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conserved nonnegative flow represented by variables on network arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a finite directed graph with source \(s\), sink \(t\), and node-arc incidence matrix \(B\) under the outflow-minus-inflow convention. An arc-flow representation of value \(\rho\geq0\) is a vector \(f\in\mathbb R_+^A\) satisfying
\[
Bf=\rho(e_s-e_t).
\]
For additive arc decision labels \(d_a\in\mathbb R^n\) and costs \(c_a\in\mathbb R\), the represented aggregate decision and cost are
\[
x=\sum_{a\in A}d_af_a,
\qquad
C=\sum_{a\in A}c_af_a.
\]
When \(\rho\in\mathbb Z_+\), requiring \(f\in\mathbb Z_+^A\) represents an integral collection of source-to-sink traversals, subject to possible cycle flows if the graph is cyclic.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An arc-flow assigns nonnegative arc values satisfying conservation, with aggregate decisions and costs obtained from additive arc labels.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite with distinguished nodes \(s\) and \(t\).
Decision labels and costs are additive over arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(Bf=\rho(e_s-e_t)\), with \(x=\sum_a d_af_a\) and \(C=\sum_a c_af_a\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The content is an appropriate arc-flow representation and explicitly acknowledges cyclic circulations. No citation or inspectable locator supports the formulation.

children.title: Path-to-Arc Projection
children.top_down_role: Structural mapping from complete path columns to aggregate arc usage.

knowledge_statements.title: Path-to-Arc Projection
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Linear projection from path weights to their induced arc flow.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite directed graph with source-to-sink path set \(\mathcal P\), define the path-arc incidence matrix \(H\in\{0,1\}^{A\times\mathcal P}\) by \(H_{aP}=1\) exactly when arc \(a\) belongs to path \(P\). The path-to-arc projection is
\[
f=Hz,
\qquad
f_a=\sum_{P\in\mathcal P:a\in P}z_P.
\]
If \(z\geq0\) and \(\sum_Pz_P=\rho\), then \(f\geq0\) and \(Bf=\rho(e_s-e_t)\). Moreover, for every additive arc vector \(w\),
\[
\sum_{a\in A}w_af_a=\sum_{P\in\mathcal P}\left(\sum_{a\in P}w_a\right)z_P.
\]
Thus the projection preserves flow value and every additive path quantity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Summing each path weight over the arcs it uses produces a conserved arc flow and preserves every additive path quantity.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal P\) consists of source-to-sink paths.
\(z\in\mathbb R_+^{\mathcal P}\) has total weight \(\rho\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f=Hz\) satisfies \(Bf=\rho(e_s-e_t)\) and preserves additive linear functionals.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The linear map and preservation identity match the path-to-arc projection container and are stated consistently. No source or specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Arc-to-Path Decomposition
children.top_down_role: Structural recovery of path mixtures from feasible network flows.

knowledge_statements.title: Arc-to-Path Decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Flow decomposition on a finite acyclic source-to-sink network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,A)\) be a finite acyclic directed graph with source \(s\), sink \(t\), and incidence matrix \(B\). If \(f\in\mathbb R_+^A\) satisfies
\[
Bf=\rho(e_s-e_t)
\]
for some \(\rho\geq0\), then there exist source-to-sink paths \(P_1,\ldots,P_k\) and coefficients \(\lambda_1,\ldots,\lambda_k>0\) such that
\[
f=\sum_{j=1}^k\lambda_j\chi^{P_j},
\qquad
\sum_{j=1}^k\lambda_j=\rho,
\qquad
k\leq |\{a\in A:f_a>0\}|.
\]
If \(f\) is integral, the coefficients may be chosen integral. Hence every feasible acyclic arc flow has a path-flow preimage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nonnegative conserved flow on a finite acyclic source-to-sink network decomposes into finitely many weighted terminal paths; integral flows admit integral weights.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite and acyclic.
\(f\geq0\) satisfies \(Bf=\rho(e_s-e_t)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(f=\sum_{j=1}^k\lambda_j\chi^{P_j}\) with \(\lambda_j>0\), \(\sum_j\lambda_j=\rho\), and integral \(\lambda_j\) when \(f\) is integral.

notation.meaning: number of paths in the decomposition

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The theorem kind is correct for this decomposition leaf, and the acyclic flow-decomposition statement, support-size bound, and integrality clause are plausible. The theorem requires an authoritative source with a specific theorem, section, or page locator.

children.title: Arc-Flow Compression Regimes
children.top_down_role: Smaller network formulations obtained through state aggregation or graph compression.

children.title: Compressed Arc-Flow Models
children.top_down_role: Arc-flow networks reduced through graph or state-equivalence compression.

assumptions_latex: \(G\) and \(\bar G\) are finite acyclic labeled networks.
The state map preserves the source, sink, arc labels, and arc costs.
\(\rho\geq0\) is the prescribed flow value.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{proj}_{x,C}F_\rho(\bar G)=\operatorname{proj}_{x,C}F_\rho(G)\) whenever labeled terminal paths map and lift in both directions with the same complete decision label and cost.

notation.meaning: flow-value-rho arc-flow formulation induced by network G, including its decision and cost projections

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quotient state network preserving terminal-path decisions through labeled lifting.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,A)\) be an exact finite acyclic labeled network, let \(\bar G=(\bar V,\bar A)\) be obtained from a source- and sink-preserving surjection \(q:V\to\bar V\), and let every image arc retain its original decision label and cost. For \(\rho\geq0\), the compressed arc-flow model uses
\[
\bar B\bar f=\rho(e_{\bar s}-e_{\bar t}),
\qquad
\bar f\geq0.
\]
Let \(F_\rho(G)\) and \(F_\rho(\bar G)\) denote the corresponding flow-value-\(\rho\) formulations, including the aggregate decision and cost equations. The compression is exact when every terminal path of \(G\) maps to a terminal path of \(\bar G\) with the same complete decision label and cost, and every terminal path of \(\bar G\) has such a lift in \(G\). Under these conditions,
\[
\operatorname{proj}_{x,C}F_\rho(\bar G)=\operatorname{proj}_{x,C}F_\rho(G).
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compressed arc-flow model quotients states and preserves the original decision-and-cost projection when terminal paths map and lift in both directions without changing their complete decisions or costs.
knowledge_statements.title: Compressed Arc-Flow Models

children.title: State-Relaxed Arc-Flow Models
children.top_down_role: Arc-flow networks reduced by merging state distinctions.

knowledge_statements.title: State-Relaxed Arc-Flow Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: State aggregation allowing all original paths and possibly additional paths.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G\) be an exact acyclic labeled network for feasible decision set \(X\), and let \(\widetilde G\) be a state-aggregated acyclic network such that every terminal path of \(G\) maps label-preservingly to a terminal path of \(\widetilde G\). Define
\[
\widetilde X=\left\{\sum_{a\in P}d_a:P\text{ is a terminal path of }\widetilde G\right\}.
\]
Then \(X\subseteq\widetilde X\), although strict inclusion may result from recombining prefixes and suffixes that were incompatible in \(G\). Consequently,
\[
\operatorname{conv}(X)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x F(\widetilde G).
\]
For minimization of any objective over \(X\), optimizing over the relaxed arc-flow projection gives a valid lower bound whenever all side constraints are relaxed consistently.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A state-relaxed network retains every original terminal path but may add paths, so its arc-flow projection is an outer relaxation useful for lower bounds.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) and \(\widetilde G\) are finite acyclic labeled networks.
Every terminal path of \(G\) has a label-preserving image in \(\widetilde G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X\subseteq\widetilde X\) and \(\operatorname{conv}(X)\subseteq\operatorname{proj}_x F(\widetilde G)\).

notation.meaning: decision labels generated by relaxed terminal paths

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly describes a state-relaxed network as an outer approximation when every original path has a label-preserving image. A specific source locator is required for the decision-diagram relaxation and bounding interpretation.

children.title: Compression-Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Compression regimes preserving the represented path or pattern set.

assumptions_latex: The network is finite, layered, and acyclic.
Only states in the same layer are merged.
Arc labels and costs are retained during the merge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(K(u)=K(v)\) for every merged pair implies equality of the complete label-cost path sets and hence equality of the induced decision-and-cost projections before and after compression.

notation.meaning: set of pairs consisting of a suffix label sequence and its additive suffix cost from state v to the terminal

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Label-and-cost completion-language condition under which same-layer state merging creates no new projected decisions or costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a state \(v\) in a finite layered acyclic labeled network, let \(K(v)\) be the set of pairs consisting of a label sequence on a path from \(v\) to the terminal and the additive cost of that suffix path. A same-layer merge is compression-equivalent when every merged pair \(u,v\) satisfies
\[
K(u)=K(v),
\]
and the merge preserves the source, terminal, arc labels, and arc costs. Under this condition, each prefix reaching either state can be continued by exactly the same label-cost suffix pairs before and after merging. Therefore the compressed network has exactly the original set of complete terminal-path label-cost pairs, and its induced path-flow and arc-flow decision-and-cost projections coincide with those of the uncompressed network.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merging same-layer states with identical label-and-cost completion languages preserves the complete terminal decisions and costs, and therefore preserves the induced path-flow and arc-flow projections onto those quantities.
knowledge_statements.title: Compression-Equivalence Regimes

children.title: Relaxation-Gap Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Boundaries where state merging admits additional network flows or columns.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Gap Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded additive gap caused by merging states with different completion languages.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a two-decision exact diagram whose terminal-path labels are
\[
X=\{(0,0),(1,1)\}.
\]
Its two states after the first decision have distinct completion languages \(\{0\}\) and \(\{1\}\). Merging them without preserving those languages creates the relaxed set
\[
\widetilde X=\{0,1\}^2,
\]
including the spurious decision \((1,0)\). For any \(M>0\), minimize \(M(x_2-x_1)\). The exact optimum is \(0\), whereas the relaxed optimum is \(-M\), attained at \((1,0)\). Thus an inexact state merge can have arbitrarily large additive relaxation gap; no instance-independent finite additive bound follows from width reduction alone.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Merging states with different suffix languages can create spurious decisions and an arbitrarily large additive optimization gap.
assumptions_latex: The two first-layer states are merged without retaining their distinct completion languages.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_{x\in X}M(x_2-x_1)=0\) while \(\min_{x\in\widetilde X}M(x_2-x_1)=-M\).

notation.meaning: terminal-decision set after the inexact merge

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary kind fits the leaf, and the explicit two-decision construction correctly produces an additive gap of magnitude \(M\). However, the record supplies neither an external citation nor an explicit standard-field rationale, so the nontrivial boundary claim lacks admissible evidence.

children.title: Decision-Diagram Interfaces

top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Chapters 3–8: Exact, relaxed, restricted diagrams, branch-and-bound, and variable ordering

children.title: Exact Decision Diagrams
children.top_down_role: Diagrams preserving the exact feasible decision set.

knowledge_statements.title: Exact Decision Diagrams
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Layered acyclic diagram representing exactly a finite feasible decision set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\) be finite. An exact decision diagram for \(X\) is a finite layered acyclic directed multigraph with root \(r\) in layer \(0\), terminal \(t\) in layer \(n\), and arcs from layer \(i-1\) to layer \(i\) labeled by elements of \(D_i\), such that
\[
X=\{(\ell(a_1),\ldots,\ell(a_n)):(a_1,\ldots,a_n)\text{ is an }r\text{-}t\text{ path}\}.
\]
Thus every root-to-terminal path encodes a feasible decision vector, and every feasible vector is encoded by at least one such path. Injectivity of the path encoding is not required unless imposed separately.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An exact layered decision diagram has precisely the feasible decision vectors as the label sequences of its root-to-terminal paths.
assumptions_latex: \(X\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\) is finite.
The diagram is finite, layered, and acyclic.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\{\ell(P):P\text{ is an }r\text{-}t\text{ path}\}=X\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition matches the exact-decision-diagram container, introduces the coordinate domains and path labeling, and correctly does not require unique path encodings. No authoritative decision-diagram source with a specific locator is supplied.

children.title: Restricted Decision Diagrams
children.top_down_role: Width-controlled diagrams retaining a feasible subset for primal bounding.

knowledge_statements.title: Restricted Decision Diagrams
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Width-controlled inner approximation retaining only feasible terminal decisions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(X\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\) and let \(W\in\mathbb Z_+\). A width-\(W\) restricted decision diagram is a finite layered acyclic diagram having at most \(W\) nodes in each decision layer and terminal-path label set \(X_R\) satisfying
\[
\varnothing\neq X_R\subseteq X.
\]
Nodes or arcs may be deleted to enforce the width bound, but no terminal path may encode an infeasible vector. Hence every diagram path supplies a feasible primal solution. For any minimization objective \(g:X\to\mathbb R\),
\[
\min_{x\in X}g(x)\leq\min_{x\in X_R}g(x),
\]
so optimization over the restricted diagram yields a valid primal upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted width-bounded diagram represents a nonempty feasible subset, so its best minimization solution is a valid primal upper bound.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) is finite and nonempty.
\(W\in\mathbb Z_+\).
The retained terminal-path set \(X_R\) is nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(X_R\subseteq X\) and \(\min_{x\in X}g(x)\leq\min_{x\in X_R}g(x)\) for every minimization objective \(g\).

notation.meaning: maximum permitted number of nodes per decision layer
decision set represented by the restricted diagram

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the restricted-decision-diagram container and correctly states the inner-approximation and minimization upper-bound properties. An authoritative restricted-decision-diagram source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Relaxed Decision Diagrams
children.top_down_role: Width-controlled diagrams containing the feasible set for dual bounding.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxed Decision Diagrams
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Layered, width-limited relaxation for a finite-domain maximization model.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\subseteq D_1\times\cdots\times D_n\) be the feasible set and let \(f(x)=\sum_{i=1}^n c_i(x_i)\). A layered acyclic diagram \(R\) is relaxed when every \(x\in F\) labels a root-to-terminal path in \(R\), while additional paths may be admitted. If each arc in layer \(i\) labeled \(a\in D_i\) has weight \(c_i(a)\), then \[\max_{x\in F}f(x)\leq \max_{P\in\mathcal P(R)}\sum_{e\in P}w_e.\] Thus a longest-path value in a width-controlled relaxed diagram is a valid upper bound; state merging must preserve path inclusion.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A relaxed diagram contains every feasible assignment, possibly with extra paths, so its longest-path value upper-bounds the maximization problem.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) is finite and every feasible assignment has a corresponding root-to-terminal path.
\(R\) is acyclic and layered by decision index.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{x\in F}f(x)\leq \max_{P\in\mathcal P(R)}\sum_{e\in P}w_e\).

notation.meaning: Root-to-terminal paths of the relaxed diagram.
Objective contribution assigned to arc e.

review_flags: Decision-diagram-specific authoritative source and exact relaxed-diagram convention are missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation and upper-bound statement fit the leaf and are mathematically plausible, but no inspectable source supports the relaxed-diagram convention or path-inclusion requirement.

children.title: Decision-Diagram Solver Interface Family

children.title: Decision-Diagram Search Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Use of decision diagrams as structured search spaces.

knowledge_statements.title: Decision-Diagram Search Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Branch-and-bound interface using restricted and relaxed diagrams at search nodes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a maximization problem, maintain an incumbent value \(L\) and a queue of partial assignments \(Q\). At a node \(u\), construct a restricted diagram whose paths are feasible completions of \(u\), obtaining a feasible value \(L_u\), and a relaxed diagram containing all feasible completions, obtaining an upper bound \(U_u\). Update \(L\leftarrow\max\{L,L_u\}\); discard \(u\) when \(U_u\leq L\). Otherwise branch on a decision or diagram state that distinguishes unresolved paths, enqueue the resulting children, and stop when \(Q=\varnothing\), returning the incumbent solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Search uses restricted diagrams for incumbents and relaxed diagrams for bounds, pruning nodes whose bound cannot improve the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: Each relaxed diagram contains every feasible completion at its search node.
Each restricted-diagram solution is feasible for the original problem.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When \(Q=\varnothing\), the returned incumbent is globally optimal.

notation.meaning: Valid upper bound at search node u.

review_flags: A decision-diagram branch-and-bound source is required for the interface and termination claim.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm fits the search-interface leaf, but global optimality additionally requires finite exhaustive branching, preservation of all feasible completions among children, and eventual processing or pruning of every node. No source is supplied.

children.title: Decision-Diagram Separation Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Use of decision diagrams to support cut or constraint separation.

knowledge_statements.title: Decision-Diagram Separation Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Longest-path separation over a diagram encoding a finite structured family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let inequalities be indexed by root-to-terminal paths \(P\) of an acyclic diagram \(D\), with path \(P\) representing \(a(P)^\top x\leq b(P)\). Given \(\bar x\), assign arc weights so that the weight of \(P\) equals \(a(P)^\top\bar x-b(P)\). Compute a maximum-weight root-to-terminal path \(P^*\). If its weight is positive, return \(a(P^*)^\top x\leq b(P^*)\); otherwise report that no inequality represented by \(D\) is violated by \(\bar x\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode each candidate inequality as a path and maximize its violation; return the maximizing inequality exactly when its violation is positive.
assumptions_latex: Every inequality in the separated family corresponds to a path of \(D\).
The chosen arc weights add to the represented inequality's violation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(P^*\) yields a most violated represented inequality, or certifies that none is violated.
review_flags: The diagram encoding and additive violation construction require a specialized source.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The longest-path separation interface is coherent, but exact certification depends on the diagram representing precisely the intended inequality family and on a valid additive violation decomposition. No source supports these specialized assumptions.

children.title: Decision-Diagram Pricing Interfaces
children.top_down_role: Use of decision diagrams as column-pricing structures.

knowledge_statements.title: Decision-Diagram Pricing Interfaces
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduced-cost pricing over paths of an exact decision diagram.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let each root-to-terminal path \(P\) of an acyclic diagram \(D\) encode a feasible column with cost \(c_P\) and master coefficients \(A_P\). Given master dual vector \(\pi\), assign additive arc weights whose path sum is the reduced cost \(\bar c_P=c_P-\pi^\top A_P\). Compute a minimum-weight root-to-terminal path \(P^*\). For a minimization master, return its column when \(\bar c_{P^*}<0\); otherwise certify that no column represented by \(D\) has negative reduced cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pricing finds a shortest diagram path under reduced-cost weights and returns its column exactly when that reduced cost is negative.
assumptions_latex: Paths of \(D\) encode exactly the columns under consideration.
Column costs and master coefficients decompose additively over arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\bar c_{P^*}=\min_{P\in\mathcal P(D)}\{c_P-\pi^\top A_P\}\).

notation.meaning: Dual vector of the restricted master problem.
Reduced cost of the column represented by path P.

review_flags: A specialized decision-diagram pricing reference is missing.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The pricing algorithm and reduced-cost formula fit the leaf, but the decision-diagram column encoding and additive reduced-cost construction lack an inspectable source.

children.title: Shared Diagram Infrastructure
children.top_down_role: Decision-diagram structures serving multiple solver roles.

knowledge_statements.title: Shared Diagram Infrastructure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common layered-DAG representation supporting search, separation, and pricing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A shared diagram infrastructure consists of a layered acyclic multigraph \(D=(V,A)\), a root \(r\), a terminal \(t\), arc labels encoding decisions, and an application-specific additive weight map \(w:A\to\mathbb R\). Its structural operations preserve layer order, path-label semantics, and root-to-terminal reachability while allowing weights to be replaced. Search bounds, separation violations, and pricing reduced costs are then computed by the same dynamic-programming recurrence \[d(v)=\operatorname{opt}_{(u,v)\in A}\{d(u)+w(u,v)\},\qquad d(r)=0,\] with the operator and weights selected by the client interface.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One layered graph and path engine can support search, separation, and pricing by changing arc weights and the path optimization operator.
assumptions_latex: \(D\) is finite, layered, and acyclic.
Each client quantity decomposes additively along root-to-terminal paths.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d(t)\) equals the client-selected optimum path weight.

notation.meaning: Optimal path weight from the root to vertex v.
Minimum or maximum, as required by the client.

children.title: Lagrangian-Subproblem Dynamic Programs
children.top_down_role: Dynamic programs solving structured subproblems created by relaxed coupling constraints.

knowledge_statements.title: Lagrangian-Subproblem Dynamic Programs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-horizon DP for a Lagrangian relaxation with separable stage transitions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider \(\min\{\sum_{i=1}^n c_i(s_{i-1},x_i):x\in X,\ \sum_{i=1}^n g_i(s_{i-1},x_i)\leq b\}\), where \(X\) is described by finite states and transitions \(s_i=T_i(s_{i-1},x_i)\). For \(\lambda\geq0\), initialize \(V_0(s_0)=-\lambda^\top b\) and set \[V_i(s)=\min_{(s',a):T_i(s',a)=s}\{V_{i-1}(s')+c_i(s',a)+\lambda^\top g_i(s',a)\}.\] Return the minimum terminal value and a predecessor path; this equals the Lagrangian subproblem value for \(\lambda\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: After dualizing coupling constraints, solve the resulting additive finite-state subproblem by a stagewise Bellman recurrence.
assumptions_latex: \(X\) has a finite-state, finite-horizon transition representation.
The objective and relaxed-constraint contributions are stage-additive.
\(\lambda\geq0\) corresponds to constraints written with \(\leq\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\min_s V_n(s)=\min_{x\in X}\{c(x)+\lambda^\top(g(x)-b)\}\).

notation.meaning: Best Lagrangian value reaching state s after stage i.

children.title: Dynamic-Programming Completion Bounds in Enumeration
children.top_down_role: DP-derived bounds embedded in partial enumeration and tree search.

knowledge_statements.title: Dynamic-Programming Completion Bounds in Enumeration
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissible DP completion bounds for pruning partial maximization states.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(u\) be a partial enumeration state with accumulated value \(g(u)\), and let \(B(u)\) be an upper bound on the value obtainable by any feasible completion of \(u\). Then \(U(u)=g(u)+B(u)\) is an upper bound on every complete solution descending from \(u\). If the incumbent feasible value is \(L\) and \(U(u)\leq L\), the entire subtree rooted at \(u\) may be discarded without removing a solution whose objective value exceeds \(L\). A backward dynamic program can supply \(B(u)\) whenever its relaxation contains all feasible completions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add an admissible DP completion bound to the partial value; prune the state when the result cannot beat the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a maximization problem.
\(B(u)\) upper-bounds every feasible completion value from \(u\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(U(u)\leq L\) implies that pruning the descendants of \(u\) cannot remove an improving solution.

notation.meaning: Objective value accumulated at partial state u.
Upper bound on the remaining completion value.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: pruning by an admissible completion bound is the standard branch-and-bound invariant; DP-specific coverage remains provisional.

children.title: Relaxation-Guided State Elimination
children.top_down_role: State pruning driven by bounds from auxiliary relaxations.

knowledge_statements.title: Relaxation-Guided State Elimination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Safe incumbent-based elimination using an auxiliary relaxation bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a maximization dynamic program, let \(g_i(s)\) be the best value of a partial path reaching state \(s\) at stage \(i\), and let \(R_i(s)\) upper-bound the value of every feasible suffix from that state. Given incumbent value \(L\), state \(s\) is safely eliminable whenever \[g_i(s)+R_i(s)\leq L.\] Indeed, every complete solution passing through \(s\) then has value at most \(L\). If \(R_i(s)\) is not a valid upper bound for every feasible suffix represented by \(s\), this elimination rule is not sound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Eliminate a state when its best prefix value plus a valid relaxed suffix bound cannot exceed the incumbent.
assumptions_latex: The problem is a maximization problem.
\(R_i(s)\) bounds every feasible suffix compatible with state \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(g_i(s)+R_i(s)\leq L\) is sufficient for safe elimination of \(s\).

notation.meaning: Best prefix value reaching state s.
Relaxation-based upper bound on a compatible suffix.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the inequality is the standard incumbent-versus-bound pruning test; a DP state-elimination source is still desirable.

children.title: DP-Based Separation Interfaces
